It was made clear to his people first. It was made clear to them and to others through their mediation, and to them he was sent first, and to them he called first and warned first. This does not mean that it was not sent to others, but if it became clear to his people, because it was in their language, it would be possible after this for anyone else to know it. His people either by learning it in their language or by explaining it in a language in which it can be understood, and the man writes a book of knowledge in medicine, grammar, or arithmetic in a language His people, then that book will be translated and transferred to other languages, and other people will benefit from it, just as the books on medicine and arithmetic were translated. It was classified by a non-Arab, and the Arabs benefited from it and knew what its authors intended, even if the one who compiled it was the first, he classified it in the language of his people. This was in explaining matters that are not related to the happiness of the afterlife and salvation from the punishment of God, so how can it be abstained from the sciences that are related to it? Happiness in the Hereafter and salvation from torment must be transmitted from one tongue to another until the people of the second language understand what the speaker intended by it. With it first, in the first tongue.

And the Muslim sons of Persia, due to their concern for this, translated many Qur’ans, writing them in Arabic and writing the translation. In Persian, and before Islam they were farther away from the Muslims than the Romans and Christians. So, the Persians, the Magi, had reached them. Meanings The Qur’an is in Arabic and its translation, so how can it not reach the People of the Book when they are closer to the Muslims than they are and the general principles that it mentions? They have evidence and counterparts in the Qur’an in the Torah, the Gospel, the Psalms, and other prophecies. Rather, everyone who contemplates prophecies He studied the prophets and pondered the Qur’an with absolute certainty that Muhammad is truly the Messenger of God and that Moses is the Messenger of God in truth, based on what he sees of the correspondence of the two Scriptures. The Torah and the Qur’an, with the knowledge that Moses - peace be upon him - did not learn from Muhammad - may God bless him and grant him peace - and that Muhammad - may God bless him and grant him peace - It was not taken from Moses, because Muhammad - may God bless him and grant him peace - according to the agreement of people who know about his condition, was an illiterate person from an illiterate people residing in Mecca. And there was no one among them who had memorized the Torah, the Gospel, or the Psalms, and Muhammad did not emerge from among them, and he never traveled except two journeys. To the Levant, he went out once with his uncle Abu Talib before he had a wet dream, and he did not separate from him, and another time with Maysarah in his business. He was the son of a woman. He spent twenty years with a group of people who knew everything about him, and he never met a scholar who learned anything from him, neither Jewish nor Christian. Nor was Buhaira or anyone else among them, but Buhaira was the monk, and when he saw him, he recognized him because of what he had of mentioning him and describing him, so he told He instructed his family to do this and ordered them to protect him from the Jews, and he did not learn a single word from Buhaira or anyone else. We will explain - that

God willing - there is a lot of evidence that he did not take a single word from any of the People of the Book and the story of Bahira that he mentioned. The masters of conduct and the authors of Musnads and Sunnahs.

Al-Hafiz Abu Issa Muhammad bin Issa bin Sura Al-Tirmidhi said in his collection: Al-Fadl Abu Al-Abbas Al-Baghdadi narrated to us, he said: Abdul narrated to us Al-Rahman bin Ghazwan Abu Nuh I am Yunus bin Abi Ishaq on the authority of Abu Bakr bin Abi Musa Al-Ash’ari on the authority of his father. He said: Abu Talib narrated To the Levant, and the Prophet - may God bless him and grant him peace - went out with him, accompanied by sheikhs from Quraysh. When they saw the monk, they came down and unhook their saddlebags, so he went out to them. Before that, they were passing by the monk, but he did not come out to them or pay attention. He said:

They were dismounting, and the monk began to move among them until he came and took the hand of the Messenger of God - may God bless him and grant him peace - and said: This is the Master of the Worlds. This is the Messenger of the Lord of the Worlds, whom God will send as a mercy to the worlds. He said: He has elders from the Quraysh. What do you know? He said: When you approached from Al-Aqaba, not a tree or a stone remained but it fell down in prostration. They do not prostrate except to a prophet, and I recognize him by the seal of the Prophethood, below the shoulder blades. Like an apple. Then he returned and prepared food for them, and when he brought it to them - and he was herding the camels - he said:

They sent for him, and he came, wearing a cloud to shade him. When he approached the people, he found that they had preceded him to the shade of the tree. When he sat down, the shade of the tree And he said: Look at the shade of the tree. He leaned over him and said: While he was standing over them, imploring them not to take him to the Romans, for the Romans If they saw him, they would recognize him by name and kill him. So he turned and saw seven Romans coming from the Romans. The monk met them and said: What brought you? They said:
We came; Because this prophet is leaving this month, there is no way left without people being sent to him, and we have been informed of his news by this way of yours.

He said, “Have you seen something that God wanted to accomplish? Can any of the people turn it away?” They said: No. He said: So they followed him and stayed with him. He said: I adjure you by God, O Arabs, which of you is his guardian? Then he said: Abu Talib, I. So he continued pleading with him until Abu Talib answered him and the monk provided him with supplies. Of cakes and oil.

Al-Tirmidhi said: This is a strange, hasan hadith. We do not know it except through this route, and Al-Bayhaqi narrated it in the book Dela’il al-Nubuwwah from the hadith of Al-Abbas. Bin Muhammad, on the authority of Qarad bin Nuh, and he said: Al-Abbas did not narrate it. By this chain of transmission, he means no one else than Qarad, and Yahya and Ahmad heard it from Qarad.
Al-Bayhaqi Arad said that no one narrated this chain of narration except these people. As for the story, it is famous among the people of the Maghazis.

Ibn Saad said in Al-Tabaqat: Muhammad bin Omar told us, he said: Muhammad bin Salih, Abdullah bin Ja’far, and Ibrahim bin Ismail bin told me. Abi Habiba, on the authority of Dawud bin Al-Husayn, said: When the Messenger of God - may God bless him and grant him peace - reached the age of twelve, Abu Talib went out to Damascus, in the caravan where he went out for trade, so they stayed with the monk Bahiri, and he said:

Bahiri told Abu Talib about the Prophet - may God bless him and grant him peace - what he said, and he ordered him to keep it. Abu Talib took it back with him to Mecca and spent the night The Messenger of God - may God bless him and grant him peace - with Abu Talib, may God protect him, protect him, and protect him from the affairs of pre-Islamic times and their faults, for whatever He wants. His dignity reached the point where he was a man who was the most chivalrous among his people, the best of them in morals, the most generous of them in sociability, and the greatest of them in forbearance. He was honest and truthful to them in speech, and kept them away from obscenity and harm. He was not seen as a gentleman or a quarrel with anyone, until his people called him the Trustworthy, according to what he gathered. There are some good things in it.
And he said:

Ibn Al-Jawzi Abu Talib went out to the Levant and with him was the Messenger of God - may God bless him and grant him peace - and he was twelve years and two months old. And for ten days, the caravan camped in Busra, where a monk - called Bahira - was in his cell. He was knowledgeable about Christianity and was still there. In that hermitage was a monk who learned the knowledge of Christianity from a young age, and there were books in it that they studied, and people would often pass by without speaking to them. Until, in that year, they camped in a house near the hermitage, and the monk prepared food for them and invited them, but he made them do so because of something he saw. When Bahiri saw that, he came down from his cell and ordered that food to be prepared and sent to the people, and he said:
O people of Quraysh, I would like to

You prepare my food, and none of you remains behind. He said: This is something you honor me. When they came to him, he began to notice the Prophet - may God bless him and grant him peace - for a moment. He looked at his body and made Abu Talib fear for him because of the monk. Then the monk said to Abu Talib, “Go back with your brother’s son, for he A being of great importance, we find his description in our books and they narrate it on the authority of our fathers. When they finished trading, Abu Talib quickly returned to Mecca, and Abu Talib did not leave with him after that, out of fear for him.

This is despite the fact that in the Qur’an there is a response to the People of the Book in some of what they distorted, such as their claim that Christ - peace be upon him - was crucified and the saying Some of them say that he is a god, and some of them say that he is a magician. They attacked Solomon - peace be upon him - and said that he was a sorcerer. Examples of this indicate that it was not taken from them.
And in the Qur’an, there are stories of the Prophets - peace be upon them - that are not found in the Torah and the Gospel, such as the story of Hud, Salih, Shuaib, and others. That.

In the Qur’an there are mentions of the Day of Resurrection and its details and descriptions of Paradise, Hell, bliss and torment, the like of which is not found in the Torah and the Gospel. The Torah does not explicitly mention the Day of Resurrection, and in general what is in it of promise and threat, it is in this world like a promise of sustenance and victory. The outcome and the threat are drought, diseases, and enemies.

Even if the mention of the Day of Resurrection exists in prophecies other than the Torah, and for this reason the People of the Book acknowledge the Day of Resurrection and the coming of the Great Resurrection. It has been said that this is mentioned in the Torah as well, but it was not explained as it was explained in other than the Torah.

chapters.title: Chapter refuting the Christians’ claim of the infallibility of the disciples who translated the Bible
paragraphs: [Chapter: Refuting the Christians’ claim of the infallibility of the disciples who translated the Bible]

If they say that the books that we have of the Torah and the Gospel and other than them were translated for us by the disciples, and they are infallible messengers with us. And they translated it for all nations, in contrast to the Qur’an, for it is only translated by those who are not infallible. There are answers to this.

One of them: This is a clear lie, for there are among the Christian Arabs the number of whom no one can count except God Almighty, and there were many Christians among them. They converted to Christianity before the sending of Muhammad - may God bless him and grant him peace - and there were among them people who followed the religion of Christ, which has not been changed, and they are believers among the people of Paradise. Like everyone else who was following the religion of Christ - peace be upon him - everyone who was following the religion of Christ, which was not changed before the sending of Muhammad, is a believer. A Muslim from the people of Paradise.

Despite this, there is neither a Torah nor an Arabized Gospel on the face of the earth from the era of the Apostles. Rather, the Hebrew Torah is transmitted from the Hebrew tongue. Or another language into Arabic. Likewise, the Gospel is transmitted from the Roman, Syriac, Greek, or other languages into Arabic. If every nation had a Torah and a Gospel and prophecies in their own language, the Arab Christians would be more deserving of this than the Abyssinian Christians. And the Saqaliba and India, for they are the neighbors of the Holy House and they are the sons of Ishmael - peace be upon him - and the Gospels are four of them, and they are They claim that everyone wrote it in a tongue. It was written in a Hebrew, Roman, and Greek tongue, although there is something in some of the Gospels that is not in others, such as Their saying:
“Baptize people in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit,” which they made the foundation of their religion, and this is what He said:

In the Gospel of Matthew, if each of the four wrote a Gospel in his own tongue, there would not be a single original Gospel to refer to. All the Gospels, and then they claim that they were translated in seventy-two languages, and this contains lies and contradictions. We will point out - God willing - some of them, but most of what they claim is that it was translated in seventy-two tongues, and it is known that the tongues What is present in the children of Adam throughout the world in our time and before our time is more than this, as those who know the conditions of the world know. One language, such as Arabic, Persian, and Turkish, is a language with different types under it, some of whom do not understand the language.

Some, unless he learns it from them, and the Arabs are the closest nations to the Children of Isaac: the Children of Israel and the Ez, for they are the Children of Ishmael. And their neighbours, for the people of Hijaz are neighbors of the Levant, and the Arabs still make pilgrimages to Mecca, and the Arabs have never had a Torah or a Gospel. Two Arabs from the era of Christ - peace be upon him - and indeed, there was neither the Torah nor the Gospel in Mecca, neither Arabized nor non-Arabized, and for this reason God Almighty said: {That you may warn a people to whom no warner has come before you} [Al-Qasas:

46] So how can it be claimed that the Torah and the Gospel were translated by the disciples for every nation of all the children of Adam, east, west, south, and north, in a different language? They understand him by it. Is anyone saying this except one of the most lying and ignorant people?

The second aspect: It is said that the translation of speech from one language to another does not require an infallible person. Rather, this is something that the nations know, as everyone who knows Two tongues make it possible for translation, and knowledge of this is achieved if the translators are many and dispersed and do not conspire in lying and with evidence. It is associated with the story of one of them and otherwise, and this exists and is known. Rather, if two people translated it, each of them did not know what he was saying:

The other, and they did not conspire, and that was what was intended in most cases, and they mentioned that the Torah was translated by seventy-two Jewish rabbis. And they were not infallible, and the king separated them so that they would not conspire in lying, and they agreed on one translation, and this was after the destruction. First, this is how it is possible to translate anything other than the Torah.

This is the Torah in our time, and the Gospel and the Psalms are translated in the Arabic language, and the meaning of them is known without a doubt, so how about the Qur’an that Do its people understand its meaning, interpret it, and translate it more fully and better than the people of the Torah and the Gospel translate the Torah and the Gospel? .
The third aspect:

The claim of infallibility in every one of the disciples, and that they are God’s messengers in the same position as Abraham and Moses - peace be upon them - is a forbidden claim. They are false, but they are the messengers of Christ - peace be upon him - in the same position as the messengers of Moses, the messengers of Abraham, the messengers of Muhammad, and most or many Christians. Some of them, or all of them, say they are messengers of God and are not prophets, and everyone who is not a prophet is not a messenger of God and is not infallible, even if he has Miraculous customs, such as the saints of God, among Muslims and others, for even if they have supernatural miracles, they are not infallible from error.

The miracles that occur at the hands of other than the prophets do not indicate that their owners are the saints of God according to most scholars, let alone Because they are infallible, the guardian of God is the one who dies with faith, and the mere fact of the supernatural does not indicate that he dies with faith, but rather he may change his mind. In this case, if we are certain that the man is a guardian of God, it is like someone who told the Prophet that he is one of the people of Paradise, then it is not necessary to believe in everything he says:

If it does not agree with what the prophets said other than the prophets - peace be upon them - then they are infallible, it is not permissible to settle on what They inform him wrongly, and for this reason God has made it obligatory to believe in them, and whoever disbelieves in any of them is an unbeliever, and whoever reviles one of them is obligatory. Killing him is according to the law of Islam, as God Almighty said: {Say, “We believe in God and in what was sent down to us and what was sent down to Abraham and Ishmael and Isaac.” And Jacob and the tribes, and what was given to Moses and Jesus, and what was given to the prophets from their Lord. We make no distinction between any of them, and to Him we submit.} [Al-Baqarah:

136] (136) {And if they believe in the same as you have believed, then they are rightly guided; but if they turn away, then they are only in discord; then God will suffice you for them, and He is the Hearer. The All-Knowing} [Al-Baqarah: 137] And God Almighty said: {The Messenger believed in what was sent down to him from his Lord, and the believers each believe in God and His angels and His books and His messengers. We make no distinction between any of His messengers. And they said, “We hear and we obey. Your forgiveness is our Lord, and to You is the return.” [Al-Baqarah: 285].
This is explained elsewhere.

chapters.title: A detailed response to their claim that God’s messengers were dispensable with the message of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace
paragraphs: [Chapter: The response to their claim that they did not need the Messengers of God to them rather than the message of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace.]

As for their saying: We are not obligated to follow him because messengers had come to us before him who spoke to us with our tongues and warned us about our religion. Which we cling to to this day, and they handed over to us the Torah and the Gospel in our language, as the book that this person brought bears witness to them. The man, where he says in Surat Ibrahim {And We did not send any messenger except in the language of his people} [Ibrahim: 4] And he said: in Surat An-Nahl {And indeed We have sent in every a nation as a Messenger} [An-Nahl: 36] The answer to him is in a number of ways: one of them:

The confirmation of a messenger before him to you does not prevent the coming of a second messenger, for the Children of Israel had sent Moses - peace be upon him - to them. They were following the law of the Torah, then God - Blessed and Most High - sent to them the Messiah - peace be upon him - and it was obligatory for them to believe in him, and whoever does not believe He was a disbeliever, even if he said so
I cling to the Book that was revealed to me.

Likewise, if God sends a messenger after Christ, it is necessary to believe in him, and whoever does not believe in him is an unbeliever, just as whoever does not believe in Christ is an unbeliever. One of the children of Israel was an unbeliever.
The children of Israel were more specific to Moses and the Torah than the Romans and others were to Christ and the Gospel, for they were Hebrews and the Torah Hebrew.
The second aspect:

Their claim that they are adhering at this time to the religion that the disciples transmitted from Christ - peace be upon him - is an obvious lie. Rather, they are in general What do they follow in terms of religion, its beliefs and laws, such as faithfulness, praying to the east, and taking pictures and statues in churches and making them methods, seeking the intercession of their companions, making festivals in their names, building churches in their names, permitting pigs, and abandoning Circumcision, monasticism, making fasting in the spring and making it fifty days, prayers, offerings, and the law were not transmitted by the disciples from The Messiah is not present, neither in the Torah nor in the Gospel. Rather, they cling to a little of what the prophets brought. Their infidelities and heresies are so many that no one has reported from Christ and the disciples that they commanded them to say what they say in Their magical prayer: “Come with us”
We prostrate ourselves to Christ our God, and in the second and third prayers: “O Mother of God, Virgin Mary, open for us the doors of mercy.”
The third aspect:

Their saying that the Torah and the Gospel were delivered to them in their languages is only valid if it is true for some Christians and not for all of them. The Arabs, both Christians and non-Arabs, no one handed over to them a Torah or a Gospel in their language, and this is a well-known matter. There has never been a Torah or a Gospel. It was Arabized from the time of the Apostles, but it was Arabized in recent times, since the Christians were Arabs, and the argument was established against them before Muhammad - May God’s prayers and peace be upon him - with a book that was sent down in a language other than theirs, then it was explained to them. So how can the argument not be established against the Romans and others by a book that was sent down in a different language? Their tongue and then translated in their tongue?

The fourth aspect: It is said that if a nation changes the religion of its Messenger that was sent to it and changes it, God will send to it someone who will call it to the religion that was sent to it. God loves him and is pleased with him, just as when the children of Israel changed the religion of Moses and changed it, God sent to them and to others the Messiah with the religion that he loves. And He is pleased with him. Likewise, when the Christians changed the religion of Christ and changed it, God sent to them and to others Muhammad - may God bless him and grant him peace - with the religion that He loves him and pleases him.

It has been proven in the Sahih on the authority of the Prophet - may God bless him and grant him peace - that he said: “Indeed, God looked at the people of the earth and detested their Arabs and non-Arabs.” Except a remnant of the People of the Book.”

And those remnants who were adhering to the religion of Christ before the sending of Muhammad - may God bless him and grant him peace - were following the religion of God - the Almighty - And since the time Muhammad - may God bless him and grant him peace - was sent, whoever does not believe in him is among the people of Hell, as he said: in the authentic hadith, “By the One who By His hand, no one from this nation, whether Jew or Christian, will hear of me, then he will die and not believe in what I was sent with, unless he will be among the companions of the Fire.” .
The fifth aspect:

That their claim may be said that the apostles delivered to them the Torah, the Gospel, and all the other prophecies in seventy-two languages, and that they will continue until Today, according to one word, there is a claim that it is known that the person who said it is speaking without knowledge, but rather an inventor and a liar. This means that he is now in These books are in seventy-two languages, all of them transmitted from the disciples, and all of them agree, not differing at all. So these are four Claims that it exists in seventy-two languages and that it is agreed upon and that it is all transmitted from the fourth disciples that they We are infallible.
It is said:

Who is there among you? If he had appreciated that these books in seventy-two languages are from the Apostles, and they exist today, who is he? It is possible for him to bear witness that they agree with each other, and that is not possible except for one who knows the seventy-two tongues and has the He knows that the scriptures were taken from the disciples, and he knows that every version in the world in this language agrees with the version he has, otherwise If he collected seventy-two versions in seventy-two languages, he would not know that each version of these is the one taken from the disciples. It is estimated that seventy-two tongues were taken from them, and it is not known that every version in the world agrees with that version, for it is known that In our time and before our time, these books were still transmitted from tongue to tongue, as they were translated from Hebrew into Arabic and from Syriac, Roman, and Greek to Arabic and others.

In that case, if a copy is found in Arabic, it is not known that it was Arabicized after the disciples or that it was taken from. The disciples, if it is assumed that an Arabic copy was taken from them, and it is not possible for anyone to collect all the Arabicized copies and compare them. We have found that the Arabized versions differ greatly from one another in translation, which prevents trust in some of them. I have seen in the Psalms several Arabized versions have such differences between them that they can hardly be understood, and what is attested to be that they have been altered, changed, and cannot be trusted. And I saw from the Torah Of the Arabized copies, many of their translations are discredited by a group of the People of the Book, so how can he gather all the copies of the two? And seventy tongues, and he compares the versions of each tongue until there is a copy in it.

the ancient ones taken from the apostles. Then he compares the versions of all the tongues, and this is only possible for someone who is familiar with both. And seventy tongues with perfect knowledge, and there is not among the children of Adam anyone who is able to do that. Even if the existence of that was estimated, it would not be known that the one who is capable of that did that. He informed us of their agreement.

If that had existed, this would have been one piece of news, or each language would have been translated by someone who knew its translation to be correct, until the translation was completed in one language. One, like an Arab, for example, and then it is known that they agree. Otherwise, if this book is translated in one or two or more languages, and the other is translated. Likewise, its agreement is not known if it is not known that the meaning of this language is the meaning of this tongue, and this can only be done by someone who knows the two languages. Or the one for whom two tongues interpret, in the tongue he knows.
It is known that no one has had the seventy-two tongues translated by one tongue or tongues that he knows, and no one is known by the seventy-two. Tongue.

In that case, the assertion that all the books written in seventy-two languages agree, or the assertion that the versions of each language agree, is an assertion that there is no It would be known to be true if it had not been on the earth today. Seventy-two tongues transmitted from the disciples were not mixed with the translator after that. So how? Most of what people have in their hands is what was translated after that into Arabic and elsewhere.

This is if it is proven that the disciples delivered it with seventy-two tongues and that it remains to this day. This is something that no one can believe. Knowing Him, today there is no Torah, Gospel, or prophecies to which anyone can attest that they were translated into the Arabic language from the era of the Apostles. Nor in most tongues, otherwise it is estimated that the disciples delivered it in seventy-two tongues even though the translation occurred after that. Due to the large number of translations, it is possible for changes to occur in some of the translations, and then the knowledge that these old versions do not change in them does not It is impossible for any change to occur in some of what was translated later or in some of what was copied from it, and there is no way to know whether it is consistent with it being two. And seventy languages other than the Qur’an, which is in the Arabic language and Arabic script. Knowledge, by agreement, of any version that exists is possible and it is preserved in The hadiths do not need to be preserved in books, as they are transmitted frequently verbally and handwritten.

The sixth aspect: Their saying, “And they delivered to us the Torah and the Gospel by our tongue, as the book that this man brought attests to them.” Then it will be said to them: There is nothing in the Qur’an that bears witness to you that the Torah and the Gospel were delivered to you through your tongue, so your citation of the Qur’an is based on This claim is similar to your citation that your religion is true.

And of the same kind as your citing of prophecies for what you narrated and with which you changed the religion of Christ - peace be upon him - from the trinity, the union, and so on. That and their saying, where God says {And We did not send any messenger except in the language of his people} [Ibrahim: 4] And He - the Almighty - said: {And We have certainly sent to every nation a messenger} [An-Nahl: 36] and it is said:

There is no doubt that the people of Moses - peace be upon him - are the Children of Israel, and in their language the Torah was revealed. Likewise, the Children of Israel are the people of the Messiah. Peace be upon him - and in their language Christ was speaking, and none of the two apostles addressed anyone except in the Hebrew language. None of them spoke Neither Roman, nor Syriac, nor Greek, nor Coptic.

And His saying - the Almighty -: {And indeed We have sent into every nation a messenger} [An-Nahl: 36] is an absolute and general statement, like His saying: {And there is no nation but within it has not passed by a warner.} [Fatir: 24] This does not undermine the fact that the Torah and the Gospel were delivered to them on their tongues.

The seventh aspect: It is said that their basis in this argument is that they say that the disciples are to us messengers of God, like Abraham and Moses. And the Messiah to us is God, and He sent these to us, so they must have been sent to us by our tongue, and they must have delivered the Torah to us. And the Gospel in our tongue.
It is said:

To them, suppose that you claim this and believe it, and we will show - God Almighty willing - that these are false claims, but you are in In this place, you will remember that this book, which is the Qur’an, which Muhammad brought - may God bless him and grant him peace - bears witness to you of this and that. It is an apparent lie against Muhammad - may God bless him and grant him peace - and his book, and you published your book that his book bears witness to you, and we show Your lies and slander against him, whether you acknowledge his prophecy or not, for it is known with certainty about him that he did not bear witness. To Christ that he is God. Rather, he has disbelieved whoever said that. He does not bear witness to the disciples that they are messengers sent by God. Rather, he only bore witness to the disciples. Because they said, “We are believers and submit,” and because they said:

We are the helpers of God, as those who believe in Him testify that they are believers and Muslims who support God and His Messenger, and that they are better than The disciples because his nation is the best of nations, as God Almighty said: {And when Jesus sensed disbelief on their part, he said, “Who are my supporters to God?” The disciples said We are supporters of God. We believe in God and bear witness that we are Muslims.} [Al Imran: 52]

And He Almighty said: {And when I inspired to the disciples, “Believe in Me and in My Messenger.” They said, “We believe.” And I bear witness that we are Muslims.} [Al-Ma’idah: 111] And He Almighty said: -: {O you who have believed, be helpers of God, as Jesus, son of Mary, said to the disciples. “Who are my supporters of God?” The disciples said, “We are.” Helpers of God, so a group of the Children of Israel believed, and a group disbelieved, so We supported those who believed against their enemy, so they became victorious} [As-Saff:

14] This will be discussed in detail, and we will explain that the messengers mentioned in Surah Yasin are not the disciples, nor were they messengers of Christ, but rather This sending took place before the Messiah, and the people of the town denied those messengers, so God destroyed them, as God Almighty said: {And what We sent down to His people after him were an army from heaven, and We would not be sent down.} [Yasin: 28] (28) {If it were but one cry, then, lo, they would be silent} [Yasin: 28]

29] The apostles mentioned in Surat Yasin are three, and there was in the town a man who believed in them, and this, even if it were Antioch, was this. The mission was before Christ, and Christ - peace be upon him - two of his companions went to Antioch after his ascension.

To heaven, and they were not reinforced by a third, and Habib the carpenter was not present at that time, and the people of Antioch believed in Christ - peace be upon him - and it was the first A city that believed in it, just as it had been spread elsewhere.

What is meant here is that Muhammad - may God bless him and grant him peace - did not bear witness to Christ’s divinity, nor to the disciples that they were messengers of God. Because they delivered to them the Torah and the Gospel with their tongue, and not that they were infallible, and what they mentioned of His saying - the Most High -: {And We did not send Messenger except in the language of his people} [Ibrahim:

4] Only the Messengers of God communicate, not the Messengers of the Messengers of God, but rather the Messengers of the Messengers of God. It is permissible for them to convey the Messengers of the Messengers in the language of the Messengers, if there is one. That language would translate for them, and if there was no one to translate that language, the messengers would speak to them in their own language, but it was not necessary for someone to This is because they wrote the divine books in their own language. Rather, it is sufficient for them to read them in the language of the prophets - peace be upon them - and then translate them. In the language of those, and He, Glory be to Him, said: {And We did not send any messenger except in the language of his people} [Ibrahim:

4] He did not say, “And We did not send any messenger except to his people.” Rather, Muhammad was sent in the language of his people, who were Quraysh, and he was sent to his people and others. His people, as they mention this about the Messiah - peace be upon him -

Chapter: As for His saying - the Most High -: {And indeed We have sent into every nation a messenger} [An-Nahl: 36], it is true and the completion of the verse: {And We have certainly sent into every nation a messenger, Worship God and avoid the tyrant, for among them are those whom God has guided, and among them are those upon whom misguidance has become certain. So travel through the earth and see what was its outcome. The deniers} [An-Nahl: 36] This is like His - the Most High - saying: In the other verse: {Indeed, We have sent you with the truth as a bringer of good tidings and a warner. And verily, there is not a nation but there has been Therein is a warner.} [Fatir: 24] And His saying: {You are only a warner, and to every people is a guide} [Al-Ra’ad:
7] In the most correct statement, that is, every people has a caller calling them to the Oneness of God.

And worship Him as you are a guide, meaning a supporter of the one to whom you are sent, and the guide means the caller, the teacher, the one who conveys the message, not the one who puts guidance in the hearts. Such as His saying: {And indeed you guide to a straight path} [Al-Shura: 52] (52) {The path of Allah, to whom belongs whatever is in the heavens and all that is on the earth} [Al-Shura: 53] And His saying: {And as for Thamud, We guided them, so they preferred blindness rather than guidance} [Fussilat:

17] It is known that the Children of Israel were the most prophetic of the nations. Moses was sent to them, and many prophets were sent after him, until it was said They are a thousand prophets, and they all enjoin the law of the Torah and do not change anything from it. Then Christ came after that with another law in which he changed it. Some of the laws of the Torah by the command of God Almighty.

If sending Moses and the prophets after him to them did not prevent sending Christ to them, then how could it prevent sending Muhammad - may God bless him and grant him peace? - To the People of the Book, the Jews and Christians, and to them since the time of Christ no messenger from God has come to them, as God Almighty said: {O People of the Book Our Messenger has come to you explaining to you, after a period of time from the Messengers, lest you say, “Neither good tidings nor warner has come to us.” Indeed, there has come to you a bringer of good tidings and a warner, by God. He has power over all things} [Al-Ma’idah:

19] This is the period that occurred between Christ and Muhammad - may God’s prayers and peace be upon them - and it is what more than one of the scholars mentioned. Like Salman al-Farisi and others, it was six hundred years, and it has been said that it was six hundred solar years, which is six hundred twenty or eighteen. This is because every hundred solar years are one hundred and three crescent years, as God Almighty said: {And they remained in their cave for three hundred years. years and more than nine} [Al-Kahf:

25] And these nine and some of the tenth, and the date on which the complete may be counted and the incomplete, so whoever says twenty will be counted according to the incomplete, and whoever says Eighteen according to the complete number only.

chapters.title: A chapter refuting their claim that God’s justice requires that they not demand the following of a person who did not come to them
paragraphs: [Chapter: A refutation of their claim that God’s justice requires that they not be required to follow a person who did not come to them]

As for their saying: We know that God is just, and it is not His justice to demand that a nation on the Day of Resurrection follow a person who did not come to them or stop them. It has a book in their language, and there is no caller on its part, so it is said: The answer is in many ways.

One of them: These words cannot be said by the one who wrote this book and no one understands Arabic, for these people understand This book is in Arabic, and they have read it and considered what is in it, and if, despite that, they understand something other than Arabic, then that is most eloquent in The proof is established for them, so they can understand what he said in Arabic and understand that to their people in the other language.

Second: They also understand what is in their Roman, Syriac, Coptic and other books and translate them for Christian Arabs. In Arabic, if the argument is established against the Arab Christians in the Roman language, then it is better for it to be established against the Romans in the Arabic language, because the Arabic language The Roman language is more widespread in the world than the Roman language, and its speakers after the emergence of Islam are more widespread than those who speak anything else, and it is more complete in its explanation. And he came to an understanding.

In that case, it will be easier for its meanings to reach people other than those who speak its language, due to the perfection of its meaning and the large number of those who know it, and these are Christian scholars. They read books on medicine, arithmetic, philosophy, and other things in the Arabic language, even though their authors were foreigners, including Romans, Greeks, and others. Therefore, what prevents the Arabic Qur’an, its interpretation, and the hadith of the Prophet - may God bless him and grant him peace - from being read in the Hebrew language, even though they were taken from The Messenger is in Arabic, so he is more likely to know the meaning of the speaker.

The third aspect: For people to be told about the justice of God in three ways. It was said: Everything that is destined is justice, and it was said: Justice is comparable to it. Justice is one of His servants, and they are two weak opinions. It was said: It is part of His justice that He rewards the doer of good deeds, without detracting from them or punishing him. Without guilt.

It is known that if a servant is commanded to do what he is able to do, it is permissible, according to the agreement of the sects of the religious sects of Muslims, Jews, and Christians, even if The act was detestable to mankind, for Paradise was surrounded by detestations and Hell was surrounded by desires. The Children of Israel and the Christians were assigned from Deeds that are hateful to them and difficult for them, so how could He refrain from commanding them and forbidding them in a language whose meaning some Muslims explain? They and the Arabs in whose tongue the Qur’an was revealed inhabited the land, and among them were countless Christians. Everyone who knew Arabic was among the Christians. He was able to understand what was said in Arabic, and whoever among them was Roman had as an example those who converted to Islam from all non-Arab sects, such as the Persians and the Turks. And the Indians, the Berbers, the Abyssinians, and others, and he is able to know what God has commanded him and to act upon it, just as all of them are empowered.

The Romans are more capable of that than others, so for what reason is it impossible for God to command them to do that, and the obligation cannot be fulfilled without it if it is It is destined for the servant, so he must do it with the agreement of the people of the Muslim sect, the Jews, and the Christians.

Rather, the people disputed over whether it should be called obligatory. It was said that it is called obligatory, and it was said that it is not called obligatory, because the commander did not intend it by the command and it may not occur to him. With his mind if the matter is created.

These people said: And because what is obligatory is what the one who abandons it is condemned according to Islamic law, or the one who abandons it is punished according to Islamic law, or what its abandoner deserves to be blamed for, or what its abandonment entails. A reason for blame or punishment, and they said: If an obligation cannot be completed without it, the one who abandons it does not deserve blame and punishment. If Hajj is obligatory, Two people, one far away and the other near, did not do it. The punishment of the far away person for abandoning it was not greater than the punishment of the relative, even though the distance between They must cut it more.

Likewise, if someone is obliged to pay off his debt without needing to sell any of his wealth, his punishment for abandonment will not be less than the punishment for abandoning it. He needs to sell his property to pay off his debt.

The conclusion of the discourse is that what the obligatory thing cannot be completed without is one of the necessities of the existence of the obligatory, and the existence of the obligatory without its necessitation is impossible. What is commanded cannot be done except by what is necessary for it, and what is forbidden cannot be done except by abandoning what is necessary for it, but this is what is necessary. It is a rational or normal necessity. Its obligation is a normal, rational obligation, not that the person himself intended to impose it and to condemn and punish for abandoning it.

People disagreed about whether it is said that an obligation cannot be completed without it. It is obligatory, whether its obligation is legally or rationally, or does it need to be said that it is not obligatory? The obligatory thing is performed only by it, and if it is within the power of the person obligated to do it, then it is obligatory? .

The public made the first statement, and some of the later ones restricted it to ability, and there is no need for that, for unless it is possible The obligation ceases with its absence, so it becomes a condition in the obligation, not in the performance of the obligation, and the majority said: The obligation cannot be fulfilled without it. It is necessary.

What is meant here is that if God made something obligatory upon His servants and the performance of the obligatory need requires learning some knowledge, then learning it is obligatory. So if the servant’s knowledge of what God has commanded him to do depends on him knowing the meaning of words spoken in a language other than his, and he is able to learn The meaning of those words that are not in his language or knowing their translation in his language is obligatory for him to learn that.

If a message came from a king to another king in a language other than his, someone would be asked to translate what the sending king meant, and it would not be permissible for him to say, “You did not.” Send me someone who speaks to me in my language, even though he is able to understand what he means by translation. How can this be said to the Lord of the Worlds? ! And if some king ordered some of his subjects and soldiers to do it in his language, and they were able to know what he ordered them to do, either by learning his language Or by someone who translates what he said to them. That was not injustice, so how could it be injustice on the part of the Lord of the worlds, even though it is not injustice on the part of the creatures? .

If it were necessary for some subjects to have rights over others or to oppress others, the king would be obliged to do justice to the oppressed and send to the oppressor someone. He commands him to do justice and fairness, and punishes him if he does not do justice, if the wrongdoer is able to know the king’s order regarding translation or otherwise. And this is justice. It is not justice for people to be left unjust to the rights of God and the rights of His servants, and God - the Almighty - sent His messengers and sent down His books. So that people may adhere to justice, as God Almighty said:

{Indeed, We have sent Our messengers with clear proofs, and We sent down with them the Book and the Balance, that the people may maintain justice.} [Al-Hadid: 25] So it is not for anyone who was sent. to him is a messenger, and he is able to know what was sent to him, with or without translation, to abstain from the law of God which he sent down, and he is The justice with which He sent His Messenger, because the Messenger’s language is not his own, despite his ability to know what he wants in multiple ways.

People, in the interest of their worldly interests, beg one of them to find out what the other wants through translation and other things, so they deal with each other, with two translators among them. They inform each other and correspond about the affairs of their countries and the purposes of their souls through the translations that they translate for them, and the matter of religion is greater than The matter of the world, so how can they not beg to know what each other wants, and how can the matter of the world be more important than the matter of religion except for those who God made his heart neglectful of the remembrance of his Lord, and he followed his desires and turned away from

chapters.title: Chapter refuting the Christian belief in crucifixion and redemption
paragraphs: He remembered his Lord and desired nothing but the life of this world. That is their level of knowledge.

God Almighty said: {So turn away from him who turns away from Our remembrance and desires nothing but the life of this world} [An-Najm: 29] And God Almighty said: {And be patient with yourself. Those who call upon their Lord in the morning and the evening desire His face, and let not your eyes turn away from them. You desire the adornments of the life of this world, and do not obey those whom We have neglected. He turned his heart away from Our remembrance, and he followed his desires, and his affair was weak.} [Al-Kahf: 28].
The fourth aspect:

It is astonishing that the Christians consider such an injustice outside of justice, even though they have attributed to God great injustice because of this. The original is what none of the nations attributed to him in the way they reviled and cursed him, accusing him of something that none of the nations cursed him with, as they are from far away. Nations from his monotheism, glorification, praise, and praise of him. This is because they claim that when Adam ate from the tree, the Lord was angry with him. And He punished him, and that punishment remained in his descendants until the Messiah came and was crucified, and that his descendants were in Satan’s prison, so who One of them died and his soul went to Hell in the prison of Satan until they said:
That is in the prophets Noah, Abraham, Moses, David, Solomon and others.
[Chapter: Refuting the Christian belief in crucifixion and redemption]

It is known that Abraham’s father was an infidel, and God did not hold him accountable for his father’s sin, so how could He hold him accountable for Adam’s sin when he was his most distant father? If it had been assumed that Adam had not repented, then how would God have informed him of his repentance?

Then they claim that crucifixion, which is one of the greatest sins and sins, through it God saved Adam and his descendants from the torment of Hell and through it He punished Satan, although Satan is still disobedient to God and deserving of punishment since he refused to prostrate to Adam and whispered to Adam until He was sent The Messiah and the Lord are able to punish him, and the sons of Adam will not be punished for the sin of their father. So who is their saying like these myths that It is a mockery of wise people, but it is not appropriate to be added to the most ignorant and most unjust of kings. So how can they claim, despite this, that they describe God? With justice, and they make it just that he does not command a person to learn what he is able to learn, and in it is his livelihood and his appointed time, and they make Such as this leads to denying His Book and His Messengers and insisting on changing the first Book and denying the other Book and that it includes Contrary to Moses, Jesus, and the other prophets and messengers?
And the Christians say: Christ, who to them is both divinity and humanity, only enabled the infidels to crucify him in order to deceive the punishment of Satan they said:

So he hid himself from the devil so that he would not know, and enabled his enemies to seize him, beat him, spit in his face, and put thorns on his head. And he crucified him, and he showed fear of death and began to say, “O my God, why have you given my enemies power over me?” so that he could hide himself from the devil, so that he would not know the devil. He is God or the Son of God, and Satan wants to take his soul to hell, just as he took the souls of Noah, Abraham, Moses, and others. The prophets and the believers. Then the Lord will protest against him and say, “Why have you made it possible for me, O Satan, to take my soul?” Then Satan says to him: Because of your sin, and he says:
My humanity is without sin, like the humanity of the prophets, for they had sins by which they deserved to have their souls taken to hell, and I I have no sin.

And they said, “When God established the argument against Satan, then it was permissible for the Lord to seize Satan and punish him and save the descendants of Adam from their perdition.” To hell, and this speech contains falsehood, and the attribution of injustice to God is too long to describe. From this is his saying: He has been defamed in the knowledge of the Lord. His wisdom and justice are something that no one has ever criticized, and that is in many ways.

One of them: It is said that Satan took the offspring because of the sin of their father, then there is no difference between the humanity of Christ and others, and if it was because of their sins, then there is no difference between the humanity of Christ and anyone else. He takes them for the sin of their father, but they said: He only took them for the sin of Adam.

Second: That it be said that whoever was created after Christ from among the descendants is like those who were created before him. So how is it possible for Satan to be empowered by the descendants of the predecessors without The later ones, and all of them were the same with regard to Adam, and they also made mistakes greater than the sins of the earlier prophets, so how is it permissible to enable Is Satan one of the punishments of the previous prophets, but he was not empowered to punish the infidels and tyrants who were after Christ? .

The third aspect: That it is said that Satan took the descendants of Adam and put them into Hell is either injustice on the part of Satan or it is... Just, if it is just, then there is no blame on Satan, and it is not permissible for him to be tricked into depriving him of the justice he deserves. Rather, he must be enabled to The latecomers and the early ones.
And if it was injustice, why did the Lord not prevent him from it before Christ? .

If it is said that he is not able, then they attribute it to inability, and if it is said that he is able to repel Satan’s injustice and he does not do it, then there is no difference between repulsing it in a certain period of time. Without time, if this is permissible, it is permissible at all times, and if it is prohibited, then it is prohibited at all times.

The fourth aspect: If Satan had an excuse before Christ, then there is no need for his punishment and he is not to be blamed, and if he was not excused, he deserved it. The punishment and there is no need for him to be deceived by a trick to establish evidence against him.

The fifth aspect: By assuming that no proof was established against him before the crucifixion, then no proof was established against him by the crucifixion, then it is possible for him to He says, “I did not know that this humanity was the humanity of the Lord, and you, O Lord, have given me permission to take all of Adam’s descendants and lead them to hell.” This is one of them, and I did not know that you or your son were united with him, and if I had known that, I would have glorified him, so I am excused in that, so it is not permissible to You treat me unjustly.

The sixth aspect: That we say: Satan then says, “O Lord, for this one human being, I made a mistake in taking his soul,” but the rest of the children of Adam Those after him, I have the right to imprison their souls in hell just as I imprisoned the souls of those who were before Christ, either because of the sin of their father or By their own sins, and then, if what the Christians say is true, then God has no argument against Satan.

The seventh aspect: That it may be said that Adam sinned and his sons sinned by accusing Satan, so the punishment of the sons of Adam for their sins is to God. Or to Satan? Would a rational person say that Satan has the right to seduce the children of Adam by beautifying them and then he has the right to punish them all without God’s permission in Is this saying anything other than the saying of the dualistic Magi who say that everything evil in the world is sins, punishment, and other things? It is the work of Satan. God did not do any of that, nor did God punish anyone for a sin.

There is no doubt that this saying was transmitted to the Christians from the Magians. That is why they do not transmit this saying in a revealed book or from any of them. The disciples, and for this reason Manichaeism was a composite religion of the religion of the Christians and the Magians, and their head was Mani, a Christian Magian, so the lineage is between The Christians, the Magians, and even all the polytheists are a well-known lineage.
The eighth aspect: It is said that Satan punished the children of Adam and caused them to enter Hell, with God’s permission or without His permission.

If they say: With His permission, then he is not guilty and does not deserve to be deceived in order to be punished and abstain, but if it was without His permission, is it permissible in justice? May God enable him to do that or not. If it is permissible in a time, it is permissible in all times, and if it is not permissible in a time, it is not permissible in all. The times, there is no difference between before Christ and after him.

The ninth aspect: It is said: Was God able to prevent Satan and his punishment without this trick, and would that have been just on his part if he had done it? Or not, if that was possible for him and it was just on his part, then he would not need to deceive Satan or crucify himself or his son, then This justice was obligatory for Satan, and if it was not obligatory, it was permissible to enable him at all times, so there is no difference between time and time.

And if it is said that he was not able to prevent Satan, then it is the inability of the Lord to prevent Satan, and this is the greatest of disbelief, according to the agreement of the people of religion. Like the dualists who say, “The light was not able to protect the darkness from evil,” and like the words of Democritus and the animists who They say that it was not possible for the necessity of existence to prevent the soul from wearing the material clothes, but rather the soul became attached to it without choosing it.
The tenth aspect:

What the Jewish infidels who crucified him did to him was whether it was obedience to God or disobedience. If it was obedience to God, then the Jews who crucified him deserved to He rewards them and honors them for their obedience to Him, just as He rewards all others who are obedient to Him. The Christians agree that those are among the people who commit the greatest sin and they are among the worst. The evil of creation, and they make lawful of their own blood and curse what they do not make lawful of others. Rather, they exaggerate in the demand of the Jews and their punishment in the end. Their fasting on days that resemble the days of the cross. And if those Jews were disobedient to God, was He able to prevent them from this? Sin or not, if he was not able, he would not be able to prevent Satan from oppressing his offspring in the future, even if he was able to He prevented them from sinning, and He did not prevent them. He would have been able to prevent Satan without this trick, and if it was good of him, he would have enabled them to This disobedience was good because it enabled Satan to oppress his offspring in the past and in the future, so there is no need to trick him.

And know that the signs that indicate the corruption of the Christian religion are very many, and whenever a rational person imagines their doctrine and imagines its requirements, it becomes clear to him. Its corruption, but what is meant here is to explain their contradiction in that they make excuses for themselves for abandoning faith in His Book, His Messenger, and His religion. Because He, Glory be to Him, is Just. He does not command people to do what they are unable to do, and He, Glory be to Him, only commands them to do what they are able to do, even though they have attributed There is injustice to him that was not attributed to him by any of the sons of Adam. This explains this.

The eleventh aspect: which is that it can either be said about injustice, according to the words of the forced Jahmiyah, who say: He does whatever He wants without Wisdom, no reason, no observance of justice. Either it can be said by the saying of Qadariyyah that he is obligated to do justice that is obligatory on creatures, or It is said that He is just and free from injustice, but His justice is not like the justice of creation. These are the sayings of the three people.
If it is said of the first, then it is permissible for Satan to have power over all the offspring without sin and to punish them all without sin or need. To trick Satan.

And if it is said about the second: then it is known that if one of the people knew that some of his mamluks had ordered others to commit a sin that the master hates, he would have done it. It is just for him to punish both the commander and the one being commanded.

As for the commander’s authority over the warden’s punishment, it is not just, nor is the unjust commander’s authority over all the descendants of the warden who did not They commit the sin of their father, which is not just.

And if it is said: Rather, he deserved to enslave them because their father obeyed him, it is said: Then he deserves to capture the first ones and the last. It is not permissible for him to be deprived of his right by defrauding him.
And if it is said: He only deserves to take them for their sins, it is said that he has the right to take the first ones and the last ones.

And if it is said: When he asked to take the soul of Christ’s humanity, he was denied this sin, it is said: If this is a sin, it is the least of his sins, for it He did not know that he was a human being of God. If a man deserved to enslave someone else’s children, he asked for a man to enslave him because he thought he was one of them. And not among them was this a sin that prevented the enslavement of the rest.

And if it is said that the Lord’s justice is not like the justice of created beings, but rather it is part of His justice that He does not detract from anyone’s good deeds and does not punish them except for their sin, it is not permissible. Then the descendants of Adam would be punished for the sin of their father, and it was not permissible for him to punish the prophets who had no sin except a sin from which they repented. Because of the sin of others, for the prophets are infallible to acknowledge a sin, so everyone of them who died died with no sin to which he was to blame. Punishment: How will they be punished after death for their father’s sin if it is estimated that he died insisting on the sin even though this is a false assessment even if it is estimated that The prophets have sins for which they deserve punishment after death, and Satan took control of their punishment, although this is a false assessment. Who after Christ, other than the prophets, is more deserving of that? How can the punishment of the prophets be permissible in the justice that requires equality between equals? And preventing the punishment of those who are inferior to them, but rather those who are among the infidels.

The twelfth aspect: If the Lord intended by this to repel Satan’s oppression, would He not unite himself with the humanity of some of Adam’s children in order to deceive Satan? So he prevents him from oppressing those who came before him, for preventing a great evil is better than preventing a little evil. Do you see that he did not know that Satan He does all this evil, so this is his ignorance, or he knew and was unable to repel it, so this is his inability. Then what is the difference between time and time? Or was abandoning his prohibition just on his part? It is just at all times.

chapters.title: The chapter on the response to the Christians in their claim is that in the words of God Almighty, “Whoever seeks a religion other than Islam is required by the Arabs alone.”
paragraphs: [Chapter: The response to the Christians in their claim that whoever is in the words of God Almighty and whoever seeks other than Islam as a religion. . . It requires the Arabs alone]

As for their interpretation of His saying - the Most High -: {And whoever seeks a religion other than Islam, it will not be accepted from him, and in the Hereafter he will be among the losers.} [Al Imran: 85] That what he wanted was his people, as they said.

As for His saying - the Most High -: {And whoever seeks a religion other than Islam, it will never be accepted from him, and in the Hereafter he will be among the losers.} [Al Imran: 85] He means according to What is required of justice is the people to whom it came in their language, not anyone else who did not bring to them what was stated in it.

So it is said to them: “Whoever interprets the meaning of a speaker” means that any speaker is in a way that people know is contrary to what he intended, then he is a liar and is slandered against, even if the speaker is From one of the common people, even if the speaker is one of the lying prophets, then if he knows that he is lying, if he speaks a word and knows what he means by it, it is not permissible If he is lied to, then it is said:

He wanted such and such, for lying is forbidden and reprehensible for everyone, whether he is truthful or a liar. So what about the one who interprets the intentions of God and His Messenger with that? Everyone who experiences his situation knows with certainty that he did not want that, but rather knows with certainty that he wanted the common thing.

For His saying - the Almighty -: {And whoever seeks a religion other than Islam} [Al Imran: 85] is a general formula, and the conditional “from” formula is one of the most eloquent forms. The general meaning is like His saying - the Most High - {So whoever does an atom’s weight of good will see it} [Al-Zalzalah: 7] (7) {And whoever does an atom’s weight of evil will see it} [Al-Zalzalah:

8] Then the context of the words indicates that he meant the People of the Book and others, for this is in Surah Al Imran during his address to the People of the Book. The Book and its discussion of the Christians, for it was revealed when the Christian delegation of Najran came to the Prophet - may God bless him and grant him peace - and he narrated that they were Sixty riders, including the Sayyid, the Ayham, and the Aqib, and their story is well-known, as mentioned above.

Before these words, he had said condemning the religion of the Christians, which they invented and with which they changed the religion of Christ and distorted the truth with which Christ was sent. With the falsehood they invented, until their religion became a mixture of truth and falsehood, and one was mixed with the other, so that there was hardly anyone with it who knew what it was. Christ abrogated the law of the Torah from what he approved, and Christ confirmed more of the law of the Torah and changed the meaning, and the general Christians do not distinguish what he decided. Whatever changed him, the religion of Christ is not known.

God Almighty said: “It is not for a human being that God should give him the Book and judgment and prophecy and then say to the people, ‘Be my servants instead of God.’” Be rabbinic in that you teach the Scripture and in that in which you study.} [Al Imran: 79] (79) And He does not command you to take the angels. And the prophets are lords. Whoever commands you to disbelieve after you have submitted?} [Al Imran: 80] It has been made clear that whoever takes the angels and the prophets He is an unbeliever, so whoever takes lords besides them is more deserving of disbelief, and it has been mentioned that the Christians took those who are without them. Lords, as He - the Almighty - says:

{They took their rabbis and monks as lords besides God and the Messiah, son of Mary, and they were not commanded except to worship one God; there is no god but It is He who is Glory be to Him above what they associate with Him.} [At-Tawbah: 31] Then He - the Most High - said: In Surat Al Imran {And when God took a covenant from the prophets, “I have given you of a Book.” And wisdom. Then there came to you a messenger confirming what is with you, so that you may believe in him and support him. He said, “Did you acknowledge it and accept my insistence upon that?” they said. We affirmed. He said, “Then bear witness, and I am with you among the witnesses.” [Al Imran: 81]

Ibn Abbas and other predecessors said: God has not sent a prophet without taking a covenant from him: If Muhammad is sent while he is alive, then people will believe in him. And let us support him, and he commanded him to take the covenant from his nation, if Muhammad were sent while they were alive, that they might believe in him, and that we should help him, and the verse It indicates what they said, for His saying - the Most High -: {And when God took a covenant with the prophets} [Al Imran: 81] refers to all the prophets {When I have given you of a Book And wisdom. Then there came to you a messenger confirming what is with you, so that you may believe in him and support him.} [Al Imran:

81] This first lam is called the lam that sets the stage for the oath, and the second lam is called the lam that responds to the oath, and the speech if a condition is met in it. And he swore, and the oath was presented, blocking the answer to the oath, blocking the answer to the condition, and the oath is as God Almighty says: {If they are driven out, they will not go out with them, even if They have been killed. They will not help them. And if they did help them, they would certainly turn back [their paths] and then they would not be helped.} [Al-Hashr: 12] And from Him - the Most High - says: {And among them are those who covenanted. By God, if He had given us of His bounty, we would certainly believe and be among the righteous.} [At-Tawbah: 75]

And His saying: {And they swore by God the best of their oaths, that if a sign came to them, they would believe in it} [Al-An'am: 109] And His saying: {And they swore by God The effort of their oaths, if I command them to go out. Say, “Do not swear.” [Al-Nur: 53] A warner, that they may be better guided than any of the nations.} [Fatir: 42] And from Him is His saying: {And if you were to ask them who created the heavens and the earth, they would certainly say, “Allah.”} [Luqman: 25] (And his saying): {And if you asked them, they would say, “We were only chatting and playing.” [Al-Tawbah: 65] (And his saying):

{If our Lord does not have mercy on us and forgive us, we will certainly be among the losers} [Al-A’raf: 149] And His saying: “If the hypocrites and those in whose hearts do not desist Sickness and those who tremble in the city - We will surely tempt you with them.} [Al-Ahzab: 60]

And His saying: {And if We willed, We could certainly follow that which We have revealed to you} [Al-Isra: 86] And His saying: {And if they do not desist from what they say, those who There will be a painful punishment among them. [Al-Ma'idah: 73] And His saying: {And if he does not do what I command him, he will surely be imprisoned and be among the despised.} [Joseph: 32] And His saying: {And if you bring to them a sign, those who disbelieve will say, “Indeed, you are nothing but vain.” [Al-Rum: 58] And His saying: {And if help came from your Lord, they would certainly say, Indeed, we were with you.} [Al-Ankabut: 10] And His saying: {And if We had delayed the punishment from them until a numbered nation, they would certainly have said, “What is keeping them back?” [Hud:
8] There are many such things, and since the oath is not mentioned, it is omitted, meaning it is appreciated.

Speech - by God - {And if they are driven out, they will not go out with them} [Al-Hashr: 12] - By God - {And if they are killed, they will not help them} [Al-Hashr: 12] Among the beauties of language The Arabs say that they omit from the speech what is indicated by the mentioned word, in short and concisely, especially in what is frequently used, such as swearing (and saying): {When I have given you of the Book and wisdom} [Al Imran: 81] This is what is conditional and decreed:

Anything I have given you of the Book and wisdom, then there comes to you a messenger confirming what you have, so that you may believe in him and support him, and do not be satisfied with what you have. of what He brought with it. And do not burden you with the Book and wisdom I have given you, so that you abandon following it. Rather, you must believe in it and support it. He was with you before him of the Book and wisdom, so what I have brought to you will not be of use to you for what he brought, for that will not save you from the punishment of God.

This indicates that whoever of the prophets and their followers meets Muhammad, even if he has the Book and wisdom, then he must believe in Muhammad. And He will support him, as He said: “When I have given you the Book and wisdom, then there comes to you a messenger confirming what is with you, that you may believe in him and support him.” [Al Imran: 81]

The prophets acknowledged this covenant, and God bore witness to it against them, as God Almighty said: {Have you acknowledged, and you have taken upon that my insistence? They said: We acknowledge. He said: So bear witness, and I am with you among the witnesses. The defiantly disobedient} [Al Imran: 82] Then He - the Almighty - said: {Do they seek other than the religion of God? When to Him have all who are in the heavens and the earth submitted, willingly or by compulsion, and to Him. They will be returned} [Al Imran: 83] Then He - the Most High - said:

{Say, “We believe in God and in what has been revealed to us, and what was revealed to Abraham and Ishmael and Isaac and Jacob and the tribes, and what was given to Moses and Jesus and the prophets.” From their Lord, We make no distinction between any of them, and to Him we submit.} [Al Imran: 84] Then He - the Most High - said: {And whoever desires other than Islam as a religion, it will not be accepted. And in the Hereafter he will be among the losers.” [Al Imran: 85]

A group of the Salaf said: When God revealed this verse, whoever among the Jews and Christians said, “We are Muslims.” Then He Almighty said: “And to God is the duty of the people to perform Hajj to the House, whoever is able to make a way to it.” [Al Imran: 97] So they said: We will not perform Hajj. Then He Almighty said: {And whoever disbelieves - God is Free from the worlds} [Al Imran: 97] So everyone who does not consider Hajj to the House obligatory for him even though he is able, is an unbeliever, according to the agreement of the Muslims, as indicated. The Qur’an is upon him.

The Jews and Christians do not see it as obligatory for them, as they are among the infidels. It was even narrated in a hadith attributed to the Prophet - may God bless him and grant him peace - “ “Whoever has provisions and a camel to bring him to the House of God and does not perform the Hajj, let him die as a Jew if he wishes, and if he wishes as a Christian.”

It is preserved from the words of Omar bin Al-Khattab - may God be pleased with him - and the Muslims have agreed that whoever denies the obligation of the principles of Islam The five Shahadas, the five daily prayers, zakat, fasting during the month of Ramadan, and the Hajj to the House, for he is an unbeliever.

And also, God Almighty said: At the beginning of the surah, “Allah bears witness that there is no god but Him, and the angels and the possessors of knowledge, standing with justice. There is no god but He, the Mighty, the Wise.} [Al Imran: 18] (18) {Indeed, the religion with Allah is Islam, and those who were given the Book did not differ except after it had come to them. knowledge out of envy among them. And whoever disbelieves in the verses of God, then surely God is quick to reckon.} [Al Imran:

19] (19) {And if they dispute with you, then say, “I have submitted my face to Allah and to those who follow me, and say to those who were given the Scripture and to the unlettered people, ‘Have you submitted?’” Indeed, they are guided, and if they turn away, then it is your duty to convey the message, and God is Seeing of His servants.} [Al Imran: 20]

God Almighty commanded him, after His saying: {Indeed, the religion with God is Islam} [Al Imran: 19] to say, “I have submitted my face to God and to those who follow them,” and to He will say to those who were given the Book, who are the Jews and Christians, and the illiterates, who are the Arabs and others who have no Book: Have you converted to Islam? The illiterate Arabs are used to use the word illiterate by common agreement.
As for others: either this word includes it, or it is included in its meaning with other words that make it clear that it was sent to All people.

He - the Almighty - said: {But if they submit, they are indeed guided; but if they turn away, then it is your responsibility only to convey the message, and God sees His servants.} [Al Imran: 20] So He commanded He brought the People of the Book to Islam as He commanded the unlettered people to do, and He made them guided when they submitted to Islam, and if they did not submit, He said: (It is upon you only Al-Baghd (the Message) means that you convey to them the messages of your Lord to them, and it is God who will call them to account. So all of this indicates that it is upon him to convey to the People of the Book. What he commanded them of Islam as he conveys to the illiterate, and that God will hold them accountable for abandoning Islam just as He holds the illiterate to account.

And in the two Sahih books on the authority of the Prophet - may God bless him and grant him peace - in the letter that he wrote to Heraclius, the king of the Christians, “From Muhammad, the Messenger of God to Heraclius Great Roman, peace be upon whoever follows guidance. As for what follows, I invite you with the message of Islam. Submit and you will be safe, and submit. May God reward you. Twice, and if you take over, you will bear the sin of the Arisians.”

And {O People of the Book, come to a common word between us and you: that we worship none but Allah, and do not associate anything with Him, and do not take lords other than God. But if they turn away, then say, “Bear witness that we are Muslims.” [Al Imran: 64] And more eloquent than that is that God Almighty has informed in His Book Islam is the religion of the prophets such as Noah, Abraham, Jacob, and their followers until the disciples, and this is the fulfillment of His saying - the Most High -: {And whoever Whoever seeks a religion other than Islam, it will not be accepted from him.} [Al Imran: 85] And the religion with God is Islam in every time and place.

God Almighty said: On the authority of Noah, the first messenger whom God sent to the people of the earth {And recite to them the story of Noah when he said to his people, “O my people, if My standing and my reminder of the verses of God are great for you, so I put my trust in God.
