114] This support by the Holy Spirit for those who support the Messengers is general in everyone who supported them over those who differed from them from the polytheists and the People of the Book, as Previously, it is not in the Qur’an, nor in the Gospel, nor in any other of the books of the prophets that the Holy Spirit with which Christ was supported is an attribute of God. It is His life, nor is the Holy Spirit a Lord who creates and provides. The Holy Spirit is not God, nor is it one of the attributes of God. Rather, it is not in anything. From the words of the prophets, the attribute of God that exists in him is called the Son, not the Holy Spirit.

If the Christians interpreted Christ’s words to baptize people in the name of the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit, the Son’s attribute is knowledge and the Holy Spirit. His characteristic, which is life, was a clear lie against Christ. There was never in his words or the words of other prophets the name of God or anything. Among his attributes is a son, nor is his life the Holy Spirit.

Also, they mention in faithfulness that Christ was incarnated by Mary and by the Holy Spirit, and this agrees with what God told us that He sent His spirit, which is Gabriel, and he is the Holy Spirit, and he breathed on Mary, and she conceived Christ, and Christ was incarnated, created from his mother and from that spirit. This spirit is not an attribute of God, nor His life, nor anything else. Rather, it is the Holy Spirit, which has been mentioned many times in the words of the prophets, and what is meant by it is either the king or the angel. Or what God places in the hearts of His prophets and guardians of guidance, support, and the like, as God Almighty said:

{Those are those in whose hearts He wrote faith and supported them with a spirit from Him} [Al-Mujadila: 22] And He - the Most High - said: {And thus We have revealed to you a spirit of Our command. You did not know what the Book or faith are, but We have made it a light by which We guide whomsoever We will of Our servants.} [Al-Shura: 52]

And He, the Almighty, said: {He sends down the angels with the Spirit of His command upon whomsoever He wills of His servants: Be warned that there is no god but Me, so fear Me.} [An-Nahl: 2] And God Almighty said: {The Possessor of the Throne sends down the Spirit of His command upon whomsoever He wills of His servants, to warn of the Day of meeting} [Ghafir: 15]. So he called the angel a Spirit. He called what the angel sends down a spirit, and they are connected, and Christ - peace be upon him - is supported by this and that.

For this reason, many commentators said that it is Gabriel, and some of them said that it is the revelation, and this, like the word of the law, means the one who has the secret of goodness, as What is meant by the spy is the one who keeps the secret of evil, so the law is Gabriel, and what is meant by him is the book that was revealed with it and what it contains of commands, prohibitions, and law. And when Waraqah bin Nawfal said to the Prophet: “This is the law that Moses used to bring.” He interpreted the law with this and that, and they go together.

chapters.title: Chapter of the response to the Christians in their protest against the verse of Surah Al-Hadid in praise of monasticism
paragraphs: [Chapter: The response to the Christians in their argument with the verse of Surat Al-Hadid in praise of monasticism]

As for His saying - the Almighty -: {Indeed, We have sent Our messengers with clear proofs, and We sent down with them the Book and the Balance, that the people may maintain justice. And We sent down iron, in it is great strength and benefits for people, and that God may know who will support Him and His messengers in the unseen. Indeed, God is Powerful, Mighty.} [Al-Hadid: 25] (25) {And We sent Noah and Abraham and placed in their descendants the prophecy and the Scripture. And among them are guided, and many of them are transgressors.} [Al-Hadid:

26] It is true as God Almighty said, and this does not include praise for monasticism nor for those who changed the religion of Christ. Rather, it is praise for those who followed him for what he made. God has mercy and compassion in their hearts, as He says: {And We placed in the hearts of those who followed Him compassion and mercy} [Al-Hadid: 27] Then He said: {And monasticism. They innovated it as We did not prescribe it for them.} [Al-Hadid: 27] That is, they invented monasticism that We did not prescribe for them. And this monasticism was not legislated by God, nor has He He makes it lawful for them, but he denied making it from them, just as he denied that from what the polytheists invented, saying:
{Allah has not made a Buhayrah, a Sa’i’ah, a Wasila, or a Ham.} [Al-Ma’idah: 103].

This definition that excludes innovations is the definition that He confirmed for the law when He - the Most High - said: {For each of you We have made a law and a course of action} [Al-Maeda: 48] And his saying: {For every nation We have appointed a ritual which they will follow} [Al-Hajj: 67] So monasticism was invented by them, God and the people did not legislate it in His statement: “and monasticism” has two opinions.

One of them: It is in the accusative case, meaning they created it either with a hidden verb that is explained by what comes after it, or this verb is said to be an action in the hidden tense. The apparent meaning is as is the saying of the Kufans. It was narrated by Ibn Jarir, Thalab and others, and its counterpart is his saying: {He admits whomever He wills into His mercy and the wrongdoers, He has prepared for them a painful punishment.} [Al-Insan: 31] And His saying: {A party He guided, and a party over whom He has confirmed the error} [Al-A’raf: 30] and upon this. The saying is that monasticism should not be based on compassion and mercy.

The second saying: She is compassionate toward her, so God has placed in their hearts compassion, mercy, and innovative monasticism, and this will be A universal creation, and the universal definition deals with good and evil, as God Almighty says: {And We made them leaders calling to the Fire} [Al-Qasas: 41]. With this saying, there is no praise for monasticism by placing it in the hearts, so it is proven according to both assessments that there is no praise for monasticism in the Qur’an.

Then he said: {Except seeking the pleasure of God} [Al-Hadid: 27] That is, it is not prescribed for them except to seek the pleasure of God, and seeking the pleasure of God by doing What he commanded, not what he created, and this is called a definite exception.

As in His saying: {They differed concerning it because there was some doubt therein. They had no knowledge of it except following conjecture, and they did not kill them} [An-Nisa: 157] And His saying - the Most High -: {O you who have believed, do not consume your property among yourselves unjustly, unless it be trade by your consent. -: {They will not taste therein death except the first death} [Al-Dukhan: 56] And He - the Most High - says: {But what is theirs is that they do not believe} [Al-Inshiqaq: 20] (20) {And when The Qur’an has been recited to them, but they do not prostrate.} [Al-Inshiqaq: 21] (21) {Rather, those who disbelieve deny} [Al-Inshiqaq: 22] (22) {And God knows best what they conceal} [Al-Inshiqaq:

23] (23) {Then give them good tidings of a painful punishment} [Al-Inshiqaq: 24] (24) {Except those who believe and do righteous deeds; they will have a reward beyond hope} [Al-Inshiqaq: 25] And His saying - God Almighty -: {They will not hear therein any idle talk or sin} [Al-Waqi’ah: 25] (25) {Except only a word, “Peace, peace.”} [Al-Waqi’ah: 26] And His saying: {And it is not for a believer to He kills a believer unless by mistake.} [An-Nisa: 92] This is the most correct statement in this verse, as it is explained elsewhere.

It is not possible for the meaning to be that God decreed it for them seeking the pleasure of God, for God does not do anything seeking the pleasure of Himself. Nor is the meaning that they invented it seeking His pleasure, as this man thinks, and this is what some of the mistaken people are, as has been explained in another place.

He mentioned that they invented monasticism and did not take care of it as it should be cared for, and that is not praise for them, rather it is condemnation. Then He Almighty said: {So We gave those who believed among them their reward} [Al-Hadid:

27] They are those who believed in Muhammad - may God bless him and grant him peace - and many of them are sinners, and if I mean those who believed in Christ also, then what is meant is: Follow him in his religion, which has not been changed. Otherwise, they all say that they are believers in Christ. In any case, God Almighty will not praise except those who follow. Christ for his religion, which has not been changed, and whoever believes in Muhammad - may God bless him and grant him peace - does not praise the Christians who changed the religion of Christ, nor those who did not believe. By Muhammad - may God bless him and grant him peace.

If it is said, some people said that His saying - the Most High -: “And monasticism they invented” [Al-Hadid: 27] is a conjunction of “compassion” and “mercy,” and the meaning is Indeed, God placed in the hearts of those who followed Him compassion and mercy, and also monasticism, which they invented and made legal and praiseworthy. It was said that this is wrong for several reasons.

Among them: that monasticism did not exist among all those who followed him, but rather those who accompanied him, such as the disciples. There was not a monk among them, but rather it was invented. Monasticism after that, unlike compassion and mercy, was placed in the heart of everyone who followed him.

Among them is that he told that they invented monasticism in a manner other than compassion and mercy. They did not invent it, and if they did, they did. He had not legislated it for them. If what was meant was the legal, religious law and not the universal, preordained law, then monasticism would not have been involved in that. If what is meant is universal moral status, then there is no praise for monasticism in that.

Among them is that compassion and mercy He placed in hearts, and monasticism is not specific to hearts, but monasticism is the abandonment of permissible matters of marriage. And meat and other things. A group of the Companions - may God be pleased with them - were interested in monasticism, so God Almighty revealed their prohibition from That is by His saying - the Most High -: {O you who have believed, prohibit not the good things that God has made lawful for you, and do not transgress. Indeed, God does not like transgressors} [Al-Maeda: 87] It is proven in the two Sahih books that “a group of the Prophet’s companions - may God bless him and grant him peace - one of them said:
As for me, I fast and do not break my fast. Another said: As for me
So I get up and do not sleep. Another said: As for me, I do not marry women. Another said: As for me, I do not eat meat.

Then the Prophet - may God’s prayers and peace be upon him - stood up and gave a sermon and said: What is the matter with men, one of whom says such-and-such, but I fast and break my fast, and get up and sleep? I marry women and eat meat, so whoever deviates from my Sunnah is not of me.”

And in Sahih Al-Bukhari, “The Prophet - may God bless him and grant him peace - saw a man standing in the sun and said: What is this? They said: This is the father of Israel. He vowed to stand in the sun and not seek shade or speak and fast. So he said: Order him to sit and take shade. And let him speak and complete his fast.”

It was proven in Sahih Muslim “on the authority of the Prophet - may God bless him and grant him peace - that he used to say in his sermon: The best speech is the speech of God and the best guidance is the guidance of Muhammad.” The worst of matters are newly invented matters, and every innovation is a misguidance.”

And in Al-Sunan on the authority of Al-Irbad bin Sariya that the Prophet - may God’s prayers and peace be upon him - said: “You must adhere to my Sunnah and the Sunnah of the Rightly Guided Caliphs, the Mahdi from After me, hold on to it and bite on it with your molars, and beware of newly invented matters, for every innovation is a misguidance.”
Al-Tirmidhi said: It is a good and authentic hadith.

Authentic texts have made clear that monasticism is an innovation and misguidance, and what was an innovation and misguidance was not guidance, and God did not give it a meaning. He legislated it as God did not legislate what the polytheists legislated, such as Buhairah, Al-Sa’i’bah, Al-Wasila, and Al-Ham.
If it is said, “He said: a group,” meaning they did not do it except to seek the pleasure of God. We did not prescribe it for them except to seek the pleasure of God.
A group said: They did not do it, or did not invent it, except seeking the pleasure of God.

It was said that both statements are wrong, and the first one appears to be wrong, as monasticism was not prescribed by God for them, but rather He did not legislate it, either by obligation or by necessity. It is desirable, but a group held that when they invented it, it was prescribed for them to complete it, and there is nothing in the verse that indicates that, for it He said: {We did not prescribe it to them except seeking the pleasure of God, but they did not take care of it as it was properly cared for.} [Al-Hadid: 27] He did not mention that he prescribed for them a soul. Monasticism, its completion, or its care, rather, it was reported that they created an innovation and that they did not take care of that innovation properly.

If it is said that His saying - the Almighty -: {So they did not care for it as it was properly cared for} [Al-Hadid: 27] indicates that if they had cared for it properly, they would have been praised.

It was said that there is nothing in the words that indicates this, but rather it indicates that, with a lack of care, they deserve censure that they do not deserve otherwise. So the blame of the one who invented the innovation and did not nurture it properly is greater than the blame of the one who fostered it, even if neither of them is praiseworthy. Reprehensible, like the Christians of Banu Taghlib and others like them who converted to Christianity and did not fulfill its duties, but rather took from it what was agreed upon. Their desires, so their disbelief and their condemnation is worse than those who are less evil than them, and the Fire has levels of levels just as Paradise has levels.
Also, when God Almighty prescribes something for His servants, He does not prescribe it seeking His pleasure. Rather, the servants do what they do seeking God's satisfaction.

Also, singling out monasticism by saying that he wrote it seeking God’s pleasure and not anything else is an unjustifiable specification, for what he wrote initially He did not mention that he wrote it seeking his approval, so how about monasticism? .

As for the statement of those who said: They did it only to seek the pleasure of God, this is the meaning. If the words indicated it, there would be no praise in that. For monasticism, whoever does what God did not command but rather forbade while having good intentions, his goal is to be rewarded for his intention, he will not be rewarded. On what is forbidden, or on what is neither obligatory nor desirable, so how, when the words do not indicate it, for God said: {We did not prescribe it to them except with the desire of God’s pleasure} [Al-Hadid: 27] And he did not say: They did it only seeking God’s pleasure, nor did he say:
They did not invent it except to seek the pleasure of God, and if that had been the intention, they would not have done it or invent it except

Seeking the pleasure of God would have been in the direct object, and he would not have introduced the verbal verb to act in it. He would not have denied innovation, but rather confirmed it. For them, only the wording of writing was presented before them, and it was known that the saying that we mentioned is the correct one and that it is a definite exception, so they appreciated it and they invented We did not prescribe monasticism for them, but we prescribe for them to seek the pleasure of God, for pleasing God is a duty written upon creation, and that is By doing what is commanded and abandoning what is forbidden, not by doing what he was not commanded to do, and abandoning what he was not forbidden from abandoning, and monasticism in it. Doing what was not commanded to do and abandoning what was not forbidden.

chapters.title: Chapter of the response to the Christians in their protest that God praised them when He said, “Among the People of the Book is an established nation.”
paragraphs: [Chapter: The response to the Christians in their argument that God praised them when He said, “Among the People of the Book is an established nation.”]

As for His saying - the Most High -: {Among the People of the Book is a standing nation, reciting the verses of God during the night, and they prostrate themselves} [Al Imran: 113] (113) {They believe. By Allah and the Last Day, and they enjoin what is right and forbid what is wrong, and they hasten in good deeds; those are among the righteous.} [Al Imran: 114] This verse is not specific to the Christians, but rather it is mentioned after His saying - the Almighty -: {You are the best of the nation brought forth for the people, giving orders. And you do what is right and forbid what is wrong and you believe in God. And if the People of the Book had believed, it would have been better for them than the believers, and most of them The disobedient ones} [Al Imran:

110] (110) {They will not harm you except harm, and if they fight you, they will turn back to you, then they will not be helped.} [Al Imran: 111] (111) {Humility has been struck upon them wherever. They were not raised except with a rope from God and a rope from the people, and they incurred the wrath of God, and calamity was struck upon them. This is because they were disbelievers. with the verses of God and kill the prophets unjustly. That is because they disobeyed and transgressed.} [Al Imran: 112] Then He said: “They are not equal from the people of The Book is an established nation} [Al Imran: 113]

It is known that the description mentioned in his saying: {That is because they used to disbelieve in the verses of God and kill the prophets unjustly} [Al Imran: 112] The characteristic of the Jews, as well as his saying: {And distress has been struck upon them} [Al Imran: 112] Then his saying after that {Among the People of the Book is a nation List} [Al Imran:

113] It must be compatible with the Jews, then the Muslims and Christians have agreed that the Jews, despite their disbelief in Christ and Muhammad - may God bless him and grant him peace peace and blessings of God be upon him - there is no believer among them and this is known by necessity from the religion of Muhammad - may God bless him and grant him peace - and the verse: “When the Christians eat food, it will be Their ruling in that matter is the ruling of the Jews, and God Almighty only praised those who believed from among the People of the Book, as He Almighty said:

{And indeed, among the People of the Book is he who believes in God and in what has been revealed to you and what was sent down to them, submissive to God who do not exchange the verses of God for a small price. These will have their reward with their Lord. Indeed, Allah is quick to reckon.} [Al Imran: 199] Most scholars have mentioned that this other verse in Al Imran was revealed about Al-Najashi and others like him who believed in the Prophet - may God bless him and grant him peace - but was not able to migrate to the Prophet - may God bless him and grant him peace. - Nor work

according to the laws of Islam, because the people of his country were Christians who did not agree with him to uphold the laws of Islam, and it was said that the Prophet - may God’s prayers and peace be upon him And peace be upon him - he only prayed for him when he died for this reason, because there was no one who would publicly pray for him in a large, visible group as he prays. Muslims at their funerals.

For this reason, he was placed among the People of the Book, despite the fact that he believed in the Prophet - may God bless him and grant him peace - in the status of one who believes in the Prophet - may God bless him and grant him peace - In a country of war, and he is not able to migrate to the land of Islam, and he is not able to work according to the apparent laws of Islam, but rather he does what he can. And what he is unable to do will be waived from him, as God Almighty said: {So if he is from a people who is an enemy to you and he is a believer, then free a believing slave} [An-Nisa’: 92] A man may outwardly be an infidel, but inwardly he is a believer, just as the people of Pharaoh were believers.

God Almighty said: {And a believing man from the family of Pharaoh who concealed his faith said, “Will you kill a man because he says, ‘My Lord is God,’ when he has come to you with clear proofs of Your Lord, even if he is a liar, then his lie is upon him, and if he is truthful, part of that which He promises you will befall you. Indeed, God does not guide one who is an extravagant liar.} [Ghafir: 28] (28) {O my people, dominion is yours today, victorious in the land. Who will help us from the might of God if it comes to us? Pharaoh said, “I will not show you except what I see.” And I guide you only to the path of right guidance} [Ghafir: 29] (29) {And he who believes says, “O my people, indeed I fear for you something like the Day of Rebellion” [Ghafir:

30] (30) {Like the habit of the people of Noah, Ad, Thamud, and those after them. And God does not intend injustice for His servants} [Ghafir: 31] (31) {And O my people, indeed! I fear for you on the Day of Calling.} [Ghafir: 32] (32) {The day you turn back, turning back. You will have no protector from God. And whoever God leads astray will have no guide.} [Ghafir: 33] (33) {And Joseph had come to you before with clear proofs, yet you remained in doubt about what he brought to you, until, when he died, you said, “God will not raise a messenger after him.” A Messenger. Thus Allah sends astray he who is extravagant and doubtful.} [Ghafir:

34] (34) {Those who dispute about the verses of God without any authority given to them are detestable to God and to those who believe. Thus does God set a seal on every heart. Arrogant and mighty} [Ghafir: 35] (35) {And Pharaoh said, “O Haman, build for me a tower that perhaps I may reach the paths”} [Ghafir: 36] (36) {The paths of the heavens So he turned to the God of Moses, and indeed I think he is a liar. And thus appeared pleasing to Pharaoh his evil deeds, and he was turned away from the path. And Pharaoh’s plan is only in ruins.} [Ghafir: 37] (37) {And he who believed said, ‘O my people, follow me. I will guide you to the right path.’” [Ghafir:

38] (38) {O my people, this life of this world is only an enjoyment, and the Hereafter is the abode of rest.} [Ghafir: 39] (39) {Whoever does evil will only be recompensed. The like of it. And whoever does righteousness, whether male or female, and is a believer - those will enter Paradise. They will be provided therein without reckoning.} [Ghafir: 40] (40) {O my people, what is the matter with me that I call you to salvation and you call me to Hell} [Ghafir: 41] (41) {You call me to disbelieve in God and associate with Him that which I have no Knowledge, and I invite you to the Mighty, the Forgiving} [Ghafir:

42] (42) {There is no doubt that whatever you call me to has no call in this world or in the Hereafter, and that we will return to God, and that the extravagant are Companions of the Fire} [Ghafir: 43] (43) {Then you will remember what I say to you, and I entrust my matter to God. Indeed, God sees His servants} [Ghafir: 44] (44) {So God protected him. The evils of what they plotted, and the evil of torment overtook the family of Pharaoh.} [Ghafir: 45] (45) {The Fire, to which they will be exposed morning and evening, and on the day when the Hour arrives, enter, all Pharaoh is the most severe in punishment.} [Ghafir: 46].

God Almighty has told us that an evil torment has befallen the family of Pharaoh, and He has told us that among the family of Pharaoh there was a believing man who concealed his faith, and that He addressed them with the speech he mentioned, for he is from the family of Pharaoh, considering lineage, gender, and appearance, and he is not from the family of Pharaoh who enter The most severe punishment. Likewise, Pharaoh’s wife is not of this Pharaoh’s family. God Almighty said, “And God sets forth as an example for those who believe, Pharaoh’s wife.” When she said, “My Lord, build for me a house with You in Paradise, and save me from Pharaoh and his work, and save me from the wrongdoing people.” [Prohibition:

11] And a man’s wife is from his family, as evidenced by his saying: {Except the family of Lot. Indeed, we will certainly save them all} [Al-Hijr: 59] (59) {Except his wife. We have decreed that she is of whom Those who left behind} [Al-Hijr: 60] And thus the People of the Book among them is who among them is outwardly and inwardly he believes in God and His Messenger Muhammad - may God’s prayers and peace be upon him. Peace and blessings of God be upon him - He does what he is able to do, and he omits what he is incapable of in knowledge and work: And {Allah does not burden a soul beyond its capacity} [Al-Baqarah: 286] He is unable to migrate to Dar al-Islam, like the inability of the Negus.

Just as those who proclaim Islam among them are those who are outwardly Muslims, and among them are those who inwardly are hypocrites and infidels, whether a Jew or Christian, polytheist, or obstructive.

Likewise among the People of the Book and the polytheists, who among them is outwardly and who is inwardly among the people of faith in Muhammad - may God bless him and grant him peace. And peace be upon him - he does what he is able to do, and omits what he is unable to do in that.

And in the hadith of Hammad bin Salamah, on the authority of Thabit, on the authority of Anas, he said: “When Al-Najashi died, he said: The Prophet - may God bless him and grant him peace - ask forgiveness for your brother, and he said Some people: You command us to ask forgiveness for this sick person who dies in the land of Abyssinia, so it was revealed: “And indeed, from the People of the Book is he who believes in God.” And what was revealed to you and what was revealed to them} [Al Imran: 199] »

Ibn Abi Hatim and others mentioned it with their chains of transmission, and Hammad bin Salamah mentioned it on the authority of Thabit on the authority of Al-Hasan Al-Basri that the Messenger of God - may God bless him and grant him peace He, peace and blessings be upon him - said: “Ask forgiveness for your brother the Negus,” and he mentioned something similar.

Likewise, a group of commentators mentioned on the authority of Jabir bin Abdullah, Ibn Abbas, Anas, and Qatada that they said: “This verse was revealed Concerning Al-Najashi, the king of Abyssinia, his name is Asahma, which in Arabic is Atiya. This is because when he died, Gabriel mourned him to the Prophet - may God bless him and grant him peace. And peace be upon him - on the day he died, then the Messenger of God - may God bless him and grant him peace - said to his companions, “Go out and pray for a brother of yours who died without Your land. They said: Who is he? He said: Al-Najashi, so the Messenger of God - may God bless him and grant him peace - went out to Al-Baqi’ and some of them added:

And it was revealed to him from Medina to the land of Abyssinia, and he saw the bed of the Negus and prayed over him and said the greatest four times and asked forgiveness for him and said To his companions: Ask forgiveness for him. Then the hypocrites said: Look at this man praying over a sick Christian Abyssinian whom he has never seen and who does not follow his religion. So it was revealed. God Almighty {And indeed, among the People of the Book is he who believes in God and in what has been revealed to you and what was sent down to them, submissive to God who do not exchange the signs of God. A small price. Those will have their reward with their Lord. Indeed, Allah is quick to reckon.} [Al Imran:

199] » A group of scholars said that it was revealed about those who followed the religion of Christ - peace be upon him - until Muhammad - may God bless him and grant him peace - was sent. Peace and blessings be upon him - so he believed in him, as was reported from Ata’.
A group held that it was revealed about all the believers of the People of the Book.

The first saying is better, for whoever believes in Muhammad - may God bless him and grant him peace - and shows faith in him is one of the people of the House of Islam. He does what Muslims do, outwardly and inwardly, then he is one of the believers, and if before that he was a polytheist who worshiped idols, then how about if he was In writing?

This is the example of Abdullah bin Salam, Salman Al-Farisi, and others. These people cannot be said to be among the People of the Book, as it is not said in The Muhajireen and Ansar are polytheists and idol worshipers, and it is not possible for any of the hypocrites or anyone else to pray on... One of them is different from those of them who are outwardly and inwardly believers.

And in the lands of Christians of this type, there are many people who conceal their faith either absolutely, or they conceal it from the public and reveal it. For their elite, and these people may be taken into account by His saying - the Most High -: {And indeed, among the People of the Book is he who believes in God} [Al Imran: 199] the verse.

These people do not claim to believe in the Book of God and His Messenger for the sake of money they take, as many rabbis and monks do. They devour people’s wealth unjustly and turn them away from the path of God, preventing them from believing in Muhammad - may God bless him and grant him peace.

As for His saying - the Most High -: {Among the People of the Book is a standing nation, reciting the verses of God during the night, and they prostrate themselves} [Al Imran: 113] (113) {They believe. By Allah and the Last Day, and they enjoin what is right and forbid what is wrong, and they hasten in good deeds; those are among the righteous.} [Al Imran: 114] This verse addresses the Jews more strongly than it does the Christians, and its counterpart is His saying - the Almighty -: {And among the people of Moses was a nation who guided with the truth. And by it they are just.} [Al-A’raf:

159] This is absolute praise for the one who adheres to the Torah. This does not include praise for the one who denied Christ, nor is it praise for the one who denied Muhammad - may God’s prayers and peace be upon him. He said hello.

This speech is explained by the context of the speech, for God Almighty said: {You are the best of peoples brought forth for mankind. You enjoin what is right and forbid what is wrong. abomination and believe in God} [Al Imran: 110]

Then He Almighty said: {And if the People of the Book had believed, it would have been better for them than the believers, but most of them are the disobedient} [Al Imran: 110]. So He made them There are two kinds: a kind of believers and a kind of sinners, and they are the majority of them. And God Almighty says: Among them are believers. Before the sending of Muhammad - may God bless him and grant him peace - as the Almighty says about them: {And We placed in the hearts of those who followed him compassion and mercy} [Al-Hadid: 27] To his saying: And many of them are transgressors, and likewise His saying - the Most High -:

{And We sent Noah and Abraham, and placed in their descendants prophecy and the Scripture; and among them are guided, and many of them are transgressors} [Al-Hadid: 26] And His saying on the authority of Abraham, the friend, {And We have blessed him and Isaac and of their descendants. He is a doer of good and no wrongdoer to himself is made clear} [Al-Saffat: 113] Then when He said: {And most of them are transgressors} [Al Imran: 110]. He said: {They will not harm you except by harm, and if they fight you, they will turn back to you, and then they will not be helped} [Al Imran:

111] (111) {Humility has been inflicted upon them wherever they find themselves, except with a rope from God and a rope from mankind, and they have incurred the wrath of God, and it has been inflicted upon them. This is because they used to disbelieve in the verses of God and kill the prophets unjustly. This is because they disobeyed and transgressed} [Al- Imran: 112]

And humiliation was inflicted on them wherever they were educated, and they did not tolerate the wrath of God and what was mentioned with it of killing the prophets unjustly and disobeying them. And their aggression was characterized by the Jews before the sending of Muhammad - may God bless him and grant him peace - as He Almighty said in Surah Al-Baqarah {And when You said, “O Moses, we will never be able to endure one kind of food, so call upon your Lord to produce for us of what the earth grows of its herbs, its cucumbers, and its garlic.” And its lentils and its onions. He said, “Will you exchange that which is better for that which is better?” Go down to Egypt, for indeed you will have what you ask for. And I have imposed on them. Humiliation and poverty. They incurred the wrath of God. This was because they used to disbelieve in the verses of God and kill the prophets unjustly. This was because They disobeyed and used to transgress} [Al-Baqarah:

61] Then he said after that {Indeed, those who believe, and those who are Jews, and the Christians, and the Sabians - whoever believes in God and the Last Day and does righteousness - for them will be Their reward is with their Lord, and there is no fear upon them, nor will they grieve.} [Al-Baqarah: 62] So this verse was addressed by those who were among the people of this sect. The four, adhering to them before abrogation without alteration. Likewise, the verse of the family of Imran when the people of

The Book by what they were characterized by. Most of them before Muhammad - may God bless him and grant him peace - were disbelievers. He said: “They are not the same from the People of the Book, a nation.” They recite the verses of God during the hours of the night and prostrate themselves.} [Al Imran: 113] (113) {They believe in God and the Last Day, and they enjoin what is right. And they forbid evil and hasten to good deeds, and those are among the righteous.} [Al Imran: 114].

This applies to those of them who were characterized by this before the abrogation, for they were following the true religion that had not been changed or abrogated, as he said in Al-A'raf {And among the people of Moses was a nation who were guided by the truth and by it they were just.} [Al-A'raf: 159] And His saying: {And We divided them into nations on earth, among them were the righteous. And among them are other than that, and We tested them with good deeds and evil deeds that perhaps they would return.} [Al-A’raf:

168] (168) {Then there succeeded a successor after them, and they inherited the Book. They take the offer of this lowest and say, “We will be forgiven, even if an offer comes to them.” They take the like of it. Was not the covenant of the Book taken from them, that they should not say about God anything but the truth, and that they should study what is in it? And the Hereafter is better for those who Do they not fear? Do you not understand?} [Al-A’raf: 169] (169) {And those who hold fast to the Book and establish prayer. Indeed, We do not waste the reward of the reformers.} [Al-A’raf: 170].

And God Almighty said: {And among those We created is a nation who guide themselves to the truth and do justice to it} [Al-A’raf: 181]. This is news from God about one who was characterized by this. Description: Before the sending of Muhammad - may God bless him and grant him peace - and whoever of these people catches up with Muhammad - may God bless him and grant him peace - and believes in him will have his reward. Twice.

chapters.title: Chapter: The response to their claim is Islam’s glorification of their temples
paragraphs: [Chapter: Refuting their claim that Islam glorifies their temples]

They said, “Then we found him magnifying our Gospel, presenting our hermitages, honoring our mosques, and bearing witness that the name of God is often mentioned in them, and that is an example.” His saying - the Almighty -: {And had God not repulsed people one by another, the silos, the shops, the prayers, and the mosques in which the name of God is frequently mentioned would have been demolished.} [Al-Hajj: 40] The answer is that it contains mention of silos and shops, and as for his saying: {Therein the name of God is mentioned frequently} [Al-Hajj: 40], it is only a mention of Him. After mentioning the mosques and mosques for Muslims, and what is meant by them is not Christian churches, for they are a sale, and then His - the Almighty - said:

The name of God is mentioned frequently in it. Either it is specific to mosques, then there is no news in that that the name of God is mentioned often in the sale. And the hermitages, or the mention of God’s name in all, there is no doubt that the hermitages and the shops before God sent Muhammad - may God bless him and grant him peace And peace be upon him - there were those who followed the religion of Christ, which had not been changed, and the name of God was mentioned in it many times, and it was said that it was after abrogation and alteration.
The name of God is often mentioned in it, and God loves for His name to be mentioned.

Al-Dahhak said that God loves for His name to be mentioned, even if He associates others with Him, meaning that the one who associates with Him is better than the obstructive, ungrateful one who does not mention His name. God is fine.

The People of the Book are better than the polytheists. We have mentioned that when Persians and the Romans fought and the Persians were victorious, that was displeased with the companions of the Messenger of God. God - may God bless him and grant him peace - and they hated the victory of the Persians over the Christians. Because Christians are closer to the religion of God than the Magians and messengers. They were sent to obtain and perfect interests and to prevent and reduce evils. And giving priority to the better of two good things over the lesser of them according to one’s ability, and repelling the evil of two evils with the good of them, so demolishing the hermitages of the Christians and selling to them is corrupt if The Magians and polytheists demolished them, but if the Muslims demolish them and turn their places into mosques in which the name of God is frequently mentioned, then this is better. And righteousness.

This verse was mentioned in the context of permission for Muslims to engage in jihad, saying - the Almighty -: {Permission is given to those who fight because they have been wronged, even though they have been wronged. God has power over their victory.} [Al-Hajj: 39] And this verse is the first verse revealed regarding jihad, and for this reason He said: “Those who were expelled from their homes without Truly, unless they say, “Our Lord is God.” [Al-Hajj: 40] Then he said: “And had God not repelled people, one of them by another.” [Al-Hajj: 40]

40] So the believers will repel the infidels and repel the evil of the two groups with the good of them, just as the Roman Magi repel the Christians. Then the Christians repel the believers as a nation. Muhammad - may God bless him and grant him peace - and this is as God Almighty said: In Surat Al-Baqarah {And David slew Goliath, and God gave him dominion and wisdom, and taught him of whatever He pleases. Had God not repulsed people one by another, the earth would have been corrupted, but God is the Possessor of bounty over the worlds.} [Al-Baqarah: 251] As for the offering in Pronunciation, as it is used to move from the lowest to the highest, as God Almighty says:

{Say, “My Lord has only forbidden immoral acts, those of which are apparent and those that are concealed, and sin and transgression without right, and that you associate with God that which He has not sent down therewith.” authority, and that you say about God what you do not know” [Al-A’raf: 33]

And His saying: {The day a man will flee from his brother, and his mother, and his father, and his wife, and his children} [Abas: 34] And his saying: {And the offspring will be offspring} [Al-Dhariyat: 1] (1) {So those who bear protection} [Al-Dhariyat: 2] (2) {So the female slaves are eased} [Al-Dhariyat: 3] (3) {So those who divide by command} [Al-Dhariyat: 4] and its counterparts are numerous.
And likewise in His saying - the Most High -: {The silos and the shops and the prayer rooms and the mosques in which the name of God is frequently mentioned} [Al-Hajj:

40] So, Glory be to Him, made it clear that had God not repelled people one by another, the places of worship would have been destroyed, and to destroy them is corruption if He destroys them. Whoever does not exchange it for something better, and the lowest of them are the silos, for the silo belongs to one person or to a small group, so he started with the lowest of the temples. He concluded with the most noble of them, which are the mosques in which the name of God is often mentioned. In general, the ruling on these temples is the ruling on their people and their people. Before the abrogation and alteration there were Muslim believers, and the demolition of the temples of the Muslim believers was corruption. After the abrogation and alteration, when the People of the Book were defeated Who is worse than them, like the Magians and polytheists, and they demolish their temples, that is corruption, and if someone who is better than them demolishes them, like a nation Muhammad - may God bless him and grant him peace - and they replaced them with mosques in which he is remembered
The name of God often, not associating anything with Him, and remembering it. Believing in all His Books and Messengers. This is righteousness, not corruption.

For this reason, the Prophet - may God bless him and grant him peace - commanded that the mosques should be used as the places of the temples of the infidels, just as the people of Taif had a temple to worship. In it are the al-Lat in which God said: {Have you seen al-Lat and al-Uzza?} [An-Najm: 19] So the Prophet - may God’s prayers and peace be upon him - ordered that that temple be demolished and taken over. Its place is the mosque in which God alone is worshipped, for indeed the mosques are the houses of God on earth. God Almighty said: {Say: My Lord has commanded justice. And establish your faces at every mosque and call upon it, sincere in religion, just as He began to return to you.} [Al-A’raf:

29] And He - the Almighty - said: {And the mosques belong to Allah, so do not call on anyone with Allah} [Al-Jinn: 18] And - Almighty said -: {It is not for the polytheists to build mosques. Allah bears witness against themselves of disbelief. Such are their works - worthless.} [At-Tawbah: 17] The verse refers to His saying: The guided ones. And He, the Most High, said: {Allah is Light. The heavens and the earth are like His light.} [An-Nur: 35] The verse refers to His saying: Without reckoning. Then when He mentioned the believers, He mentioned the disbelievers from the People of the Book. And the polytheists, and He mentioned the people of ignorance, whether simple or complex, and He, Most High, said:

{And those who disbelieve, their deeds are like a mirage in a valley, which the thirsty person thinks is water; until when he comes to it, he does not find it to be anything, but he finds God with him, and He pays him his account. And God is quick in reckoning.} [An-Nur: 39] (39) {Or like the darknesses in a deep sea covered by waves, and above them are waves of darkness, some of which are clouds of darkness. On top of another, when he takes out his hand he can hardly see it. And for whomever God does not make light, he has no light.} [An-Nur: 40] It has become clear that they have no light. An argument for something that Muhammad - may God bless him and grant him peace - brought. Rather, what he brought is an argument against them in multiple ways.

chapters.title: A chapter rejecting their claim that they must adhere to their religion after the mission of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace
paragraphs: [Chapter: Rejecting their claim that it is obligatory to adhere to their religion after the mission of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace.]

They said, “This and other things obligated us to adhere to our religion and not neglect what we have, nor reject our doctrine, nor follow anyone other than the Lord Christ.” The Word of God, His Spirit, and His disciples whom He sent to us.

The answer is that they used two false arguments: One of them is that Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, was not sent to them, but to the Arabs. It has become clear that using it as evidence is one of the greatest lies and slanders against Muhammad - may God bless him and grant him peace - as he never said that I was not sent to People of the Book, nor did he ever say, “Indeed, I was not sent except to the Arabs.” Rather, his texts transmitted from him and his actions show that he was sent to all The people of the earth are their unlettered and their written.
The second argument: their saying:

That Muhammad - may God bless him and grant him peace - praised the religion of the Christians after they had changed and abrogated, and this is also a greater lie against him than the one before it. How? He praises them, but he declares them to be unbelievers in more than one place in his book, and he commands their jihad and fighting them, and he condemns those who neglect their jihad to the fullest extent. He criticizes and describes those who do not see his obedience in fighting them as hypocrisy and disbelief, and mentions that he will enter Hell, and all of this is reported on the authority of God. He mentions it to convey the message of his Lord, but it is added to it; Because he conveyed it and performed it, not because he created it and initiated it.

As He - the Almighty - said: {Indeed, it is the word of a noble Messenger} [Al-Haqqah: 40] (40) {And it is not the speech of a poet. Little do you believe} [Al-Haqqah: 41] (41) {And do not By the word of a soothsayer: Little do you remember.} [Al-Haqqah: 42] (42) {A revelation from the Lord of the worlds} [Al-Haqqah: 43] (43) {Even if he uttered some words against us} [Al-Haqqah: 44] (44) {We would certainly have taken from him by the right hand} [Al-Haqqah: 45] (45) {Then We would have cut off from him the two jaws} [Al-Haqqah: 46] (46) {And there is not one of you who can withhold from him} [Al-Haqqah: 47] (47) {And indeed, it is a reminder for the righteous} [Al-Haqqah: 48] (48) {And indeed, we know that among you are deniers} [Al-Haqqah: 49] (49) {And indeed, it is a regret. upon the disbelievers} [Al-Haqqah:
50] (50) {And indeed it is the truth of certainty} [Al-Haqqah: 51] (51) {So glorify the name of your Lord the Great} [Al-Haqqah:

52] As for the praise of God and His Messenger for the Messiah and his mother and for those who followed him and followed his religion that has not been changed, this is true and it is not contradictory. The obligation of following Muhammad - may God bless him and grant him peace - on whoever was sent to him, even if it were assumed that the law of Christ had not been changed and that Muhammad - may God bless him And peace be upon him - he praised everyone who followed it and said, however, that God has sent me to you. This was not contradictory, and if he who did not believe in him disbelieved, he would not This contradicts his praise of them before they disbelieved him.

So how could he, when he only praised those who followed a religion that had not been changed? As for those who changed the religion of Christ, he did not praise them, but rather disparaged them, as he said: “And among those who said, ‘We are Christians,’ We took their covenant, but they forgot by chance.” From what they were reminded with, So We caused among them enmity and hatred until the Day of Resurrection. And God will inform them of what they used to do.} [Al-Maeda: 14] We have presented that the Christians disbelieved just as the Jews disbelieved: they disbelieved because they changed what was in the first book, and they disbelieved because they disbelieved in the second book.

As for those who did not change the Book or catch up with Muhammad - may God bless him and grant him peace - and believe in him, then these are believers, and what this shows is that glorifying Christ’s devotion to the Torah, his following of it, and his doing of its laws is greater than Muhammad’s veneration of the Gospel, may God bless him and grant him peace. This would be a waiver of the Jews’ obligation to follow Christ, so how could Muhammad’s glorification of the Gospel, may God bless him and grant him peace, be a waiver of the obligation? Christians must follow it.

chapters.title: Chapter refuting the Christians’ claim that Islam glorified the disciples
paragraphs: [Chapter: Refuting the Christians’ claim that Islam venerates the disciples]

As for their saying: And his disciples whom he sent to us warned us in our language and entrusted to us our religion, who have been exalted in this book. By saying in Surat Al-Hadid: {Indeed, We have sent Our messengers with clear proofs, and We sent down with them the Book and the Balance so that the people may maintain justice} [Al-Hadid: 25] And he said in Surah Al-Baqarah {So God sent the prophets as bearers of good tidings and warnings, and sent down with them the Book with the truth to judge between the people concerning what they differed about} [Al-Baqarah: 213] So I mean by his saying:

His missionary prophets and messengers imitate those disciples who went around in seven regions of the world and preached the one Book, which is The pure Gospel; Because if it were meant on the authority of Abraham, David, Moses, and Muhammad, he would have said: They have the Scriptures; Because each one of them brought a book without

He changed it and did not say anything except the one book. Because no group came bringing good tidings of one book except the Apostles who brought the pure Gospel, and it also came in the Book {and it came from At the furthest end of the city is a man running. He said, “O my people, follow the messengers.” [Yasin: 20] meaning the disciples. He did not say “messenger.” Rather, he said: “messengers,” and the answer. In many ways: one of them:

There is nothing in what was mentioned or in anything else that requires you to deny the Messenger who was sent to you and to others and to adhere to a changed and abrogated religion as That nothing in which Moses, the Torah, or those who followed Moses are glorified is something that requires the Jews to deny the Messenger who was sent to them and to adhere to a religion. Altered and copied.

Second: That their saying: We do not follow anyone but Christ and his disciples is false, for they are not followers of either Christ or his disciples for two reasons: One of them: Their religion is a change, not all of it is from Christ and the disciples, but most of their laws, or many of them, are not from Christ. And the disciples.

Second: That Christ gave good tidings about Ahmed, as God Almighty said: {And when Jesus, son of Mary, said, “O Children of Israel, indeed I am the Messenger of God to you, confirming what before me of the Torah and bringing good tidings of a messenger who will come after me, whose name is Ahmad} [As-Saff: 6].

If they do not follow Ahmad, then they are denying Christ, and they have some good news about Christ and other prophets regarding Ahmad. It will be explained in another place, as will come - God willing.

Rather, what is meant here is to prevent them from using anything that Muhammad - may God bless him and grant him peace - brought as evidence and to clarify that it is an argument against them and not for them. Because they claimed that there was evidence for them in some of it.

Third: Their saying about the disciples that they are the messengers who are glorified in this book is a false statement with which they interpreted the Qur’an in a false way. The type of their interpretation: “Those upon whom You have bestowed grace” [Al-Fatihah: 7] are Christians. Their interpretation is by my permission, meaning that it is blown into and it becomes a bird, with the permission of the divinity, which is the word of God united in humanity. And their interpretation: {This is the Book} [Al-Baqarah: 1] with the Gospel, and their interpretation: {Those who believe in the unseen and establish prayer and of what We have provided them They spend} [Al-Baqarah:
3] (3) {And those who believe in what was revealed to you and what was sent down before you, and are certain of the Hereafter} [Al-Baqarah: 4] are the Christians.
Their interpretation is His saying: {And do not dispute with the People of the Book except in a way that is best} [Al-Ankabut: 46] They are the Christians.
{Except those who are wrong} [Al-Ankabut: 46] They are the Jews.

Examples of this are their interpretation of the Qur’an, just as they use them to interpret the Torah, the Gospel, and the Psalms, among the interpretations that are a distortion of the word. About its circumstances, and atheism in the verses of God, and lying to His prophets, in what appears to be a lie to the prophets, to everyone who ponders that. The invalidity of this appears in many ways.

One of them: that God said: {We have sent Our messengers with clear proofs, and We sent down with them the Book and the Balance so that the people may adhere to justice, and We sent down Iron contains great strength and benefits for people, and that God may know who will support Him and His messengers in the unseen. Indeed, God is Powerful, Mighty.” [Al-Hadid: 25]. And His saying - the Almighty -: {Indeed, We have sent Our messengers} [Al-Hadid: 25] is a genitive plural noun that includes everyone whom God Almighty has sent.

Second: That the Messengers were more deserving of this ruling than those whom he named in the Qur’an. As God Almighty said: {Indeed, We have revealed to you just as We revealed to Noah and the prophets after him, and We revealed to Abraham and Ishmael and Isaac. And Jacob, and the tribes, and Jesus, and Job, and Jonah, and Aaron, and Solomon, and We gave David the Psalms - and messengers whom We have narrated to you before, and messengers who have not We related them to you, and God spoke to Moses specifically - messengers bringing good tidings and warnings, so that people might not have any argument against God after the messengers. And God is mighty. Wise} [An-Nisa: 163-165]

If the Messengers of Muhammad - may God bless him and grant him peace - were not given the name of the Messenger of God in the book he brought, then how is it permissible to say: This name refers to the messengers of another messenger, and what is meant here is to clarify the meanings of the Qur’an and what God - Blessed and Most High - intended by saying: {When The messengers came to it when We sent to them two} [Yasin: 13].

Do what God and His Messenger Muhammad - may God bless him and grant him peace - mean are those whom God sent or those whom His Messenger sent, when it is known with certainty that Muhammad did not Something like this includes whoever says: Muhammad - may God’s prayers and peace be upon him - intended by that the one whom he sent as a messenger. He has lied to Muhammad - may God’s prayers and peace be upon him. Peace be upon him - intentionally or accidentally.

chapters.title: A chapter explaining the corruption of their saying in the interpretation of the verse of Surat Al-Baqarah. So God sent the prophets as bearers of good tidings and warnings
paragraphs: [Chapter: Explaining the corruption of their statement regarding the interpretation of the verse of Surat Al-Baqarah. So God sent the prophets as bringers of good tidings and warnings.]

It has become clear from what we have mentioned that their saying: in interpreting the verse of Al-Baqarah is corrupt, for they said: And He said: in Surat Al-Baqarah {So God sent the prophets Bringing good tidings and warnings, and He sent down with them the Book with the truth, that He might judge between the people concerning that in which they differed.} [Al-Baqarah: 213] They said: So by His saying I mean: His prophets. The missionaries and His messengers are similar to the disciples who traveled in seven regions of the world and preached the Book, which is the pure Gospel. Because if I meant about Abraham, Moses, David, and Muhammad, he would have said:

And with them were the books; Because each one of them brought one book and not another, and only said one book. Because no group came preaching one book except the Apostles who brought the pure Gospel.
It is said to them: Some evidence has been presented that indicates the falsity of this interpretation.
Also, God Almighty said: “The people were one nation” [Al-Baqarah: 213], that is, they differed. {So God sent the prophets as bearers of good tidings and warnings} [Al-Baqarah: 213].

The disciples are not among the prophets, even though Christ sent them, and His sending of them does not necessitate that they be prophets like those sent by Moses. And Muhammad and others. This is why most Christians call them messengers and do not call them prophets.
Also, he said: And He sent down the Book with them.

As for the disciples, the Book was not sent down with them. Rather, the Book was sent down with Christ, but the prophets were with them the type of the Book. Al-Kitab is a generic noun, and it includes all the revealed books. As in His saying: {But righteous is he who believes in God and the Last Day and the angels and the Scripture and the prophets} [Al-Baqarah: 177] and in His saying: {Everyone believes. By God and His angels and His books and His messengers} [Al-Baqarah: 285] And in the other reading (and His Book and His messengers), and likewise His saying about Mary: {And she believed in the words of her Lord and His Books} [Prohibition:
12] And in the other reading (and his book) and also - God Almighty - said: {People were one nation, so God sent the prophets as bringers of good tidings and warnings} [Al-Baqarah: 213].

And He - the Almighty - said: In Surah Yunus {And mankind were not but one community, and they differed} [Yunus: 19]. This indicates that when the children of Adam differed, God sent The prophets, and their difference, occurred before Christ, before Moses, before Hebron, even before Noah. As Ibn Abbas said: Between Adam and Noah there were ten centuries, all of them following Islam, then polytheism and disagreement occurred among them on two sides at times. They disagree, some of them believe and some of them disbelieve. As God Almighty said:

{And if God had willed, those after them would not have fought each other after clear proofs had come to them, but they differed. Some of them believed and some disbelieved.} [Al-Baqarah: 253] And God Almighty said: {These are two adversaries who have disputed over their Lord} [Al-Hajj: 19] meaning the people of faith and disbelief, and it may be that all of them disagree on False, as he said:

{And those who differ concerning the Book are in far-flung discord} [Al-Baqarah: 176] And His saying: {And they do not cease to differ, except on whom your Lord has mercy} [Hud: 118] And also: The Gospel does not contain a ruling between people regarding what they disagreed about, but rather it contains sermons, commandments, and news of Christ, in contrast to the Torah and the Qur’an. In them there is a ruling between the people regarding what they disagreed about, which is not in the Gospel.

And also, he said: {And none differed therein except those who were given it after the clear proofs had come to them, out of envy among themselves. So God guided those who believed to what They differed concerning the truth by His permission} [Al-Baqarah: 213].

This implies that God guided those who believed after the disagreement of those who were given the Scripture out of envy among themselves because they differed concerning the truth, and this is reprehensible. For those who were given the Scripture and differed.

The Christians are included in this condemnation, and if what was meant was the Gospel, they would be the ones to be blamed to the exclusion of anyone else. This is not the case, but rather the Jews and others. Those who differ are also reprehensible, but those who are praised are the believers whom God guided for the truth about which they differed, by His permission.

This definitely applies to the nation of Muhammad - may God bless him and grant him peace. It may also apply to all of the advanced nations who believed, such as those who followed the religion of Moses. And Christ and Abraham the friend; As God Almighty said: {Indeed, those who believe, and those who are Jews, and the Christians, and the Sabians - whoever believes in God and the Last Day and does righteousness - for them will be Their reward is with their Lord, and there is no fear upon them, nor shall they grieve.} [Al-Baqarah:

62] As for the nation of Muhammad - may God bless him and grant him peace - God guided them to the truth regarding what the nations before them differed about, by His permission, and this It is clear, for they adhere to truth and justice, the middle ground between the two extremes of falsehood, and this is evident in their following the truth about which the Jews and Christians differed. In monotheism, prophets, news, legislation, abrogation, permissible and forbidden, ratification, disbelief, and other than that.

As for monotheism, the Jews likened the Creator to the created being, and described the Lord, Glory be to Him, with the imperfect attributes that are unique to the created being. They said: God is poor and stingy and He gets tired and other things.

The Christians described the creation with the attributes of the Creator, the attributes of perfection that the Creator specializes in, and they said: About Christ, that he is the Creator of the heavens. And the earth, the Ancient and Eternal, Knower of the Unseen, Able to do all things, and: “And they took their rabbis and monks as lords besides God” [At-Tawbah: 31] The verse.

And the Muslims, God guided them regarding the truth about which they differed. They did not liken the Creator to the created being, nor the created being to the Creator, but rather they confirmed to God what He deserves His attributes of perfection and His being free from shortcomings, and they acknowledge that there is no one like Him and no one is equal to Him in any of His attributes. Perfection, so they freed Him from shortcomings, unlike the Jews, and from the resemblance of creation to Him, unlike the Christians.

As for the prophets - peace be upon them - the Jews killed some and denied others. As God Almighty said: {Is it that whenever a messenger comes to you with anything your souls do not desire, you become arrogant, and you deny a group, and you kill a group} [Al-Baqarah: 87].

And the Christians associated themselves with themselves and with those besides them, so they worshiped Christ. Rather, they took their rabbis and monks as lords besides God and made The disciples were messengers of God, and they claimed that by obeying Him man would become in the position of the prophets, and they depicted the statues of the prophets and the righteous, and they became They call upon them and seek their intercession after their death, and when a righteous man among them dies, they build a mosque over his grave and place their statues in it.

And in the two Sahih books, “The Prophet - may God bless him and grant him peace - mentioned to him a church in the land of Abyssinia, and he mentioned its beauty and the pictures in it, and he said: Those are the ones who, when a righteous man among them dies, build a mosque over his grave and depict those images in it. Those will be the worst of creation in the sight of God on the Day of Judgment. “The Resurrection.”

As for the Muslims, God guided them to the truth regarding what was disputed, by His permission, so they believed in all of God’s prophets and did not differentiate between any of them. They did not go as far as the Christians did, nor were they negligent in their rights as the Jews were. Likewise, the Jews killed those who commanded justice from the people. Christians obey those who command polytheism, and polytheism is a great injustice, and they obey those who forbid what is permissible and permit what is forbidden, and Muslims obey those who He commands obedience to God, but they do not obey those who command disobedience to God.

And the Christians among them are polytheists in God, and the Jews among them are arrogance in worshiping God. As God Almighty said: Concerning the Christians: “They took their rabbis and monks as lords besides God and the Messiah, the son of Mary, and they were not commanded except to worship One God; there is no god but He. Glory be to Him above what they associate with Him.} [At-Tawbah: 31] And He said: Concerning the Jews: {Is it that whenever a messenger comes to you with anything your souls do not desire? You were arrogant, and a group you denied, and a group you killed} [Al-Baqarah:

87] Islam is that the servant submits to God alone and worships Him alone according to what He has commanded him to do. So whoever submits to Him and to others is A polytheist, and God does not forgive anyone who associates anything with him. And who?

He did not submit to Him, but rather became arrogant in worshiping Him. He was among those about whom it was said: “Call upon Me, I will respond to you. Indeed, those who are too arrogant to worship Me.” They will enter Hell, humiliated.} [Ghafir: 60] For this reason all the prophets and their nations submitted to God, worshiping Him alone according to what He commanded them to do. Even if their laws varied, the Messiah was still a Muslim because he was following the law of the Torah and when God made a copy of it for him.

And Muhammad remained a Muslim when he prayed towards the Holy House, then when he prayed towards the Kaaba and when God sent him to the creation, they were all They were commanded to obey Him, and the worship of God was obedience to Him, so whoever did not obey Him was not a worshiper of God and was not a Muslim.
As for legislation, the Jews claimed that what God commanded He forbids Him to abrogate.

The Christians claimed that what God commanded made it permissible for their elders to abrogate it, so God guided the believers to the truth about what they differed about, so they said: God, Glory be to Him, has the right to abrogate what He has legislated, unlike the Jews, and it is not for a created being to change anything of the Creator’s law, unlike the Christians.

As for what is permissible and what is forbidden, purity and impurity, the Jews were forbidden from good things, and the matter of impurities was made more difficult for them, to the point that they were forbidden. Of eating with a menstruating woman, of sitting with her in a house, and of removing impurity, and it was forbidden to them the fat of the otter, the kidneys, and everything that has nails and other things. That.
And Christ - peace be upon him - made lawful for them some of what was forbidden to them, so the Christians met them and said:

There is nothing forbidden, neither pig nor anything else, nor anything impure, neither urine nor anything else. They claimed that some of their elders saw a sheet on which he was photographed. Pictures of animals, and it was said to him, “Eat what pleases your soul and leave what you dislike,” and that all animals were permitted to them, and they abrogated the law of the Torah simply by That is, what is permissible to them is what their souls desire, and what is forbidden to them is what their souls dislike. So God guided those who believed to what The truth was differed from it, so God made lawful for them the good things and forbade for them the evil ones and removed from them the burdens and shackles that were on the children of Israel, in contrast to the Jews, and He commanded them to purify both impurity and impurity, in contrast to the Christians.

The Jews made the Messiah - peace be upon him - born of adultery, a liar and a sorcerer, and the Christians made him God, the Creator of the heavens and the earth. So God guided those who They believed in the truth about which they differed, by His permission.

So they testified that he is the servant of God, a created being unlike the Christians, and that he is a noble messenger in this world and the hereafter, and one of those who are close to him, unlike the Jews. Believing and disbelieving, for the Jews are in the habit of disbelieving the truth, and the Christians are in the habit of believing in falsehood, for the Jews are disbelievers. Who among the prophets they denied when they brought the truth; As God Almighty said: {Is it that whenever a messenger comes to you with anything your souls do not desire, you become arrogant, and a party you deny, and a party you kill} [Al-Baqarah:
87] And the Christians believe in the absurdities of reason and laws; They also believed in trinity, unity, and similar abstentions.

chapters.title: Chapter on responding to their statement that the Qur’an bears witness to them that they are supporters of God
paragraphs: [Chapter: The response to their statement that the Qur’an bears witness that they are helpers of God]

Then they said: On the authority of the Qur’an that it bears witness to them that they are helpers of God, where it says: Just as Jesus, son of Mary, said: Who are my helpers to God? He said: {The disciples, we are the helpers of God, so a group of the Children of Israel believed and a group disbelieved, so we supported those who believed against their enemy. So they became apparent.} [As-Saff: 14] It is said:

This is true, and the disciples are believers and Muslims, and they are supporters of God, but this does not mean that they are messengers of God, nor does this mean that everything You are based on the religion taken from them, and it is not in this that one of the disciples is infallible from error. Rather, God commanded the believers from a nation Muhammad - may God bless him and grant him peace - to be supporters of God; As Christ requested this by saying: “Who are my helpers to God?” [As-Saff: 14].

God has described the believers, the Companions of the Prophet - may God bless him and grant him peace - from the people of the Prophet’s City as being helpers of God, according to His saying - the Almighty: -: {And the forerunners, the first among the immigrants and the Ansar, and those who followed them in righteousness, may God be pleased with them and they are pleased with Him} [At-Tawbah: 100] The Muhajireen are better than the Ansar, and they are also among the Ansar of God. They helped him; The Ansar also supported him, but since they had a name of their own, which is Al-Muhajiroun, which is the better of the two names, the Ansar were singled out for this. Name.
The Muhajireen and Ansar are better than those who believed in Moses and those who believed in Jesus according to the Muslims.
Despite this, there is neither a prophet nor a messenger of God among them, but among them are the messengers of the Messenger of God - may God bless him and grant him peace - in peace.

chapters.title: The chapter on responding to them regarding their claim that Islam exalts the Gospel that is in their hands
paragraphs: [Chapter: The response to their claim that Islam magnified their Gospel which was in their hands]

Chapter They said: As for his glorification of our Gospel and our books that are in our hands, he says: {And We sent down to you the Book with the truth, confirming what was before it} [Al-Ma’idah: 48] And he said: In Surah Al Imran: {M - Allah, there is no god but He, the Ever-Living, the Ever-Subsisting - He has sent down to you the Book in truth, confirming what was before Him and sent down The Torah and the Gospel - before, a guidance for mankind} [Al Imran: 1-4]. And he said:

In Surat Al-Baqarah {L-M - This is the Book in which there is no doubt, a guidance for the righteous - those who believe in the unseen and establish prayer, and spend out of what We have provided them - And those who believe in what was revealed to you and what was sent down before you and are certain of the Hereafter - those are upon guidance from their Lord, and those are they. The successful ones} [Al-Baqarah: 1-5]. So by the Book I mean the Gospel and those who believe in the unseen. We

Christians who believed in Christ and what we saw, then he followed by saying {And those who believe in what was revealed to you and what was revealed before you} [Al-Baqarah: 4] So by them I mean the Muslims who believed in what he brought and what came before him. And He said: in Surat Al-Ma’idah {And an admonition to the righteous - and may He judge. The people of the Gospel according to what God has revealed in it, and whoever does not judge by what God has revealed - those are the disobedient.” [Al-Ma’idah: 46-47] And he said in Surah Al Imran: {Then if they deny you, then indeed have been denied messengers before you who brought clear proofs and the Psalms and the Book that enlightens} [Al Imran:
184] I also mean by the enlightening book, which is the Holy Bible.

He also said: {And if you are in doubt about what We have revealed to you, then ask those who read the Book before you. Indeed, the truth has come to you from your Lord, so do not You will be among those who doubt.} [Yunus: 94].
So what was with us was confirmed by this, and the accusations, alterations, and changes of what was in them were banished from our Gospel and our books that are in our hands by his believing them.

The answer: After you know that the wording of the first verse of Surat Al-Ma’idah {And We have sent down to you the Book with truth, confirming what was before it Of the Book and having dominion over it} [Al-Ma’idah: 48]. That it should be said: As for the confirmation of the Seal of the Messengers, Muhammad, the Messenger of God - may God bless him and grant him peace - in what God sent down before him of the Scriptures and for those who came before him. Prophets, this is known by the apparent frequency of his religion, like the frequency of sending him to all of creation, and this is one of the principles Faith.

God Almighty said: {Say, “We believe in God and in what was sent down to us, and in what was sent down to Abraham and Ishmael and Isaac and Jacob and the tribes and what was given.” Moses and Jesus and what was given to the prophets from their Lord - We make no distinction between any of them, and to Him We submit - so if they believe in the like of what you have believed in, then They are guided, and if they turn away, then they are only in discord, so God will suffice for them, and He is the Hearing, the Knowing.} [Al-Baqarah: 136-137] And He - the Most High - said:

{Say, “We believe in God and in what has been revealed to us, and what was revealed to Abraham and Ishmael and Isaac and Jacob and the tribes, and what was given to Moses and Jesus and the prophets.” From their Lord, We make no distinction between any of them, and to Him we submit - and whoever desires a religion other than Islam, it will not be accepted from him, and in the Hereafter he will The losers} [Al Imran: 84-85]

And he said: {Righteousness is not that you turn your faces towards the east and the west, but righteousness is he who believes in God and the Last Day and the angels and the Scripture. And the Prophets, and He gave money out of love for Him to relatives, and orphans, and the needy, and the wayfarer, and the beggars, and for freeing slaves, and established prayer, and paid zakat. And those who fulfill their covenant when they pledge, and those who are patient in hardship and adversity and in times of hardship. These are the ones who are truthful, and it is they who are righteous.} [Al-Baqarah: 177]

And He Almighty said: {The Messenger believed in what was sent down to him from his Lord, and the believers each believe in God and His angels and His books and His messengers. We make no distinction between anyone. Of His messengers, and they said, “We have heard and obeyed. Your forgiveness, our Lord, and to You is the return.” Our Lord, do not hold us accountable if we forget or make a mistake. Our Lord, and do not place upon us a burden as You placed upon those before us. Our Lord, nor You burden us with what we cannot bear, and pardon us, and forgive us, and have mercy on us, You are our Master, so help us against the disbelieving people} [Al-Baqarah:

285 - 286] And his confirmation of the Torah and the Gospel is mentioned in places in the Qur’an, and He said: {And We have sent down to you the Book with the truth, confirming what is His hands are of the Book, and He has dominion over it.} [Al-Ma’idah: 48].

And He Almighty said: {Allah has sent down the best of hadith, a book similar to it, repeated over and over} [Az-Zumar: 23] And He said: {We narrate to you the best of stories by what We have revealed. Here is the Qur’an.} [Joseph:

3] So he made it clear that He sent down this Qur’an as a dominant over the books that were before it, and the dominant is the witness, the trustworthy, the arbiter, who bears witness to what is in them. the truth, and denies what has been distorted in it, and rules by confirming what God has approved of its rulings, and abrogates what God has abrogated from it, and he is trusted in That was against her and he told that he had the best hadith and the best stories, and this implies that he was everyone who adhered to the Torah before the abrogation. Without changing any of its rulings, he is among the people of faith and guidance, and so is he who adheres to the Gospel without changing it. Some of his rulings were before abrogation, so he is one of the people of faith and guidance, and in that there is no praise for one who adheres to a changed law, let alone one who adheres to it. With an abrogated law, and he did not believe in what God had sent to him of the messengers or the Scriptures sent down to him. Rather, he demonstrated the disbelief of the Jews and Christians by changing The first book: And abandoning belief in Muhammad - may God bless him and grant him peace - in more than one place.

As for their interpretation of His saying: {That is the Book} [Al-Baqarah: 2] that it is the Gospel and {those who believe in the unseen and establish prayer and of what We have provided them They spend} [Al-Baqarah: 3]

What the Christians meant by them is that it is distorting words from their proper place and changing the word of God. Just as they did in His saying: {And whoever desires other than Islam as a religion} [Al Imran: 85] and in His saying: By My permission, that is, by divinity, and in His saying: {Guide us The straight path} [Al-Fatihah: 6].
